# Jantt Production-Readiness Plan

_Generated 2026-11-16. Source: an 18-scope parallel code audit (each scope read in full by a dedicated auditor; 12 scopes additionally re-checked by an adversarial verifier, which refuted 5), plus open GitHub issues. **771 findings** are tracked below as checkbox tasks. Nothing is committed; all work stays in the working tree until the owner signs off._

## 1. Executive summary

Overall state. Jantt covers a lot of ground: a framework-agnostic Gantt engine with a staged schedule pipeline, CPM/PERT/Monte Carlo/EVM/levelling, six bindings, MS Project/P6/CSV interop, a canvas renderer, CLI, MCP server, Python bridge, and a React playground with Firebase cloud rooms. It is not production-ready. The verified audit has 771 findings: 10 critical, 132 high, 376 medium and 253 low. By category that is 92 false-logic, 70 data-loss and 94 security or rules-security findings, and `npm test` is red on main because of a date time-bomb in packages/core/tests/integration.test.ts. Some parts are solid and worth keeping: the core's shape (pipeline stages, gesture strategies, separate renderer modules, a JSON plan model with a schema), the breadth of the package set, a working lockfile/CI/release scaffold, and a reconciliation layer whose 3-way design is sound in outline. Four things are dangerous. The cloud layer is live with public PII and rules that were patched one clause at a time; commit 52ec345 still leaves the editor branch comparing non-leaf val() values. Common sync paths silently lose edits. Renderers put plan data into innerHTML in a product that shares plans between users. And a large set of features give confident but wrong answers, or claim guarantees the code does not provide. That includes the product's core value, a correct schedule. All paths in this plan are relative to D:/Repos/Jantt.

Top risks, ranked. (1) RTDB rules and PII. An unauthenticated GET of /users.json returns every account's uid, email and GitHub handle (RULES-02/FBSVC-08). Usernames can be squatted and profiles impersonated. Presence can be spoofed in any room. Removed members can rejoin as viewers. The editor rule compares non-leaf val() values, so editors either can rewrite the roster or cannot save. The secretKey is world-readable. No node has type/size validation or $other guards, and the rules are neither tested nor deployed by CI. (2) Sync data loss. calculatePlanHash ignores priority, milestone, locked, costs, baselines, custom fields and more, so those edits are never pushed and are overwritten by remote snapshots (ROOMSYNC-02/ARCH-01). Beyond that: the merge base is overwritten by the local autosave; pending saves are cancelled on room switch or tab close; edits made during an in-flight save are dropped; field LWW falls back to task-level timestamps; tombstones are capped at 50. Locally, share links delete same-named plans, undo writes plan A into plan B, multiple tabs overwrite each other, dragging a cloud room onto Local deletes it without confirmation, and reopening Notes blanks the open note. (3) Stored, cross-user XSS. It is zero-click through category/person/team colors in the grid table, tooltip and sidebar. It also reaches the command palette's dangerouslySetInnerHTML, note mention pills, the CLI and Python HTML templates, and unvalidated Yjs remote data. The validator does no type checks on render-sensitive fields, and there is no CSP. (4) False logic in the scheduling core. Cycles push dates months further out on every resolve, and the shifted dates get saved. The CPM uses a 0-day gap while the cascade uses 2 days, so the drawn critical path is wrong. SS/FF/SF links and lags are flattened by ordinary edits. A zero lag cannot be expressed. Working calendars never reach the cascade. The Beta-PERT sampler is U-shaped. EVM invents budgets and reports SPI 1.0 when there are no costs. The leveler defers the highest-priority task. The canvas 'critical path' toggle highlights urgent tasks. Edit links, team sharing, cross-tab sync, 'zero data loss', 'CRDT/commutative' and 'off-main-thread' are not real. (5) Build and release. The CSS export paths in core and standalone point to files the build does not emit. The Dockerfile is broken. The Node engine floor is wrong (Node 20 has been EOL since April 2026). Lint is a no-op, and npm audit can never fail CI.

What 'production ready' means for each surface. Core library: one scheduling convention (inclusive end, typed links with expressible zero lag, calendars honored, cycles reported rather than cascaded); a CPM that matches the drawn schedule; honest analytics that show 'n/a' instead of invented numbers; sanitizePlan at every boundary plus escaping in every sink; an explicit public API; onError and diagnostics; a drag fast path and virtualization within stated budgets; CSS exports that exist. Playground app: no silent data loss (flush on switch/close/hide, per-project storage, truthful save status, visible quota errors); error boundaries; a single commit gateway that enforces read-only and feeds a per-plan undo; the four owner UX asks; one dialog/popover system; a WCAG 2.2 AA baseline; a CSP; code splitting. Cloud rooms: least-privilege rules proven by an emulator test matrix; no public PII; an explicit visibility model; revision-CAS commits on the data node only; honestly documented merge semantics with conflicts shown to the user; presence moved off the room node; revocation that sticks; existing rooms migrated. Bindings: correct CSS paths, core as a peer dependency, SSR-safe elements, no full remount churn, and a Yjs binding that diffs against a base, carries every section and validates remote data. CLI/MCP/Python: a localhost-only token-protected server, escaped HTML, correct exit codes, MCP protocol compliance (isError, ping, notifications), NaN-safe pandas conversion, one version source. CI/release: green on Node 22/24; real ESLint (including no-unsanitized); rules emulator, Playwright/axe and size-limit gates; audit gating; lockstep 2.0.0 with provenance and all-or-nothing publish; a working Docker image.

Sequencing. Day 0: I recommend the owner approve one out-of-band hotfix: lock /users reads to the record's owner and scrub stored emails. It is the only item that should not wait for the full cycle, because the exposure is live. Phase 0 (contracts first): freeze the cross-cutting APIs as typed stubs with tests: sanitizePlan, contentHash, TASK_SYNC_FIELDS/stampTaskChanges, plan-ops, the dependency-graph API, date conventions, planStore/commitPlan, the roomRepository interface and SyncError, the Modal/Popover/Menu props, urlState, and the rules model. Phase 1: nine workstreams code in parallel, each with exclusive file ownership (core scheduling/analytics; core render/interaction; reconciliation plus the playground sync engine; rules, Firebase services and migration; playground state/storage/URL/shell; playground UI system and owner UX asks; bindings/interop/canvas; CLI/MCP/Python/worker; build/CI/release/docs). Each workstream's review starts as soon as its coding ends. Phase 2: the global gate (build, typecheck, lint, unit, rules emulator, Playwright/axe, size budgets), then owner sign-off, and only then commits. Rollout order: a client release compatible with both rule sets, then the RTDB migration, then new rules deployed from CI, then a minClientVersion bump, then removal of the shims.

Guardrails against complexity (deliberate non-goals). No Cloud Functions dependency. The design is rules-only and states its limits: there are no per-user room quotas, so App Check plus usage alerts stand in for them. RTDB rooms do not get a real CRDT; they stay a server-serialized 3-way merge, and @jantt/yjs remains the CRDT option. No state-management library, DI container or event bus. No new packages beyond moving Firebase and remote-fetch concerns out of core. The secret-key 'edit link' model is replaced by owner-granted roles and access requests rather than made more elaborate. Mechanical directory renames inside core are deferred to a post-gate PR so they cannot cause merge conflicts between parallel workstreams.

## 3. Architecture decisions

1. LAYERING (ARCH-08). Four layers, with dependencies pointing one way only. (1) @jantt/core is the pure plan model, scheduling, analytics and DOM renderer, with no network calls, no Firebase and no window.__JANTT_* globals. Delete packages/core/src/firebase-sync.ts: its REST /plans room API is denied by the rules (RULES-05/ARCH-07), and the playground's signed-out REST path goes with it. Move its RTDB key codec to apps/playground/src/firebase/rtdbCodec.ts and fix it there: the __schema collision, empty-array restore and __proto__ keys. Move remote-sync.ts to an opt-in subpath export @jantt/core/remote that requires a proxyUrl option; the author's personal worker is no longer the default. (2) apps/playground/src/lib holds framework-free TypeScript: urlState, storage, ids, identity, download, errors. (3) apps/playground/src/firebase holds the only modules that import the Firebase SDK, loaded lazily with dynamic import. (4) React hooks and components. Core's index.ts replaces `export *` with an explicit, documented export list, and internals are marked @internal.
2. CANONICAL CORE MODULES (duplicates resolved). (a) scheduling/graph.ts buildDependencyGraph(tasks) returns typed edges with lags, a topological order, SCC cycles and duplicate ids. The validator, CycleGuardStage, CascadeResolveStage, cpm, hasDependencyCycle, monte-carlo, the leveler and schedule-health all use it. Delete the Kahn copies in resolver.ts, cycle-guard-stage.ts and cpm.ts and the recursive DFS in validator.ts. (b) resolveSchedule becomes a thin wrapper over SchedulePipeline.createDefault(), so there is one cascade entry point, and it returns diagnostics. (c) date-math.ts is the only module that computes durations or the FS minimum start. (d) plan-ops.ts provides deleteTask, setDependencies, addLink and removeLink: immutable, preserving link types and lags, and writing tombstones. It replaces the four delete implementations (useTaskDetailSidebar, TaskScheduleCoordinator, controller.handleKeyDown, TasksView) and the dependsOn flattening in sanitize-stage, link-gesture and sidebar. (e) sidebar.ts is the only task editor; delete detail-modal.ts and the createDetailModal export. (f) reconciliation/fields.ts holds TASK_SYNC_FIELDS and stampTaskChanges(prev, next, clock), used by playground stamping, task-merger and hashing; delete PM_TRACKED_FIELDS from useEditorState. (g) content-hash.ts contentHash(plan) is a stable canonical JSON of the whole plan minus volatile keys. It replaces calculatePlanHash everywhere (sync, snapshot dedup, meta.contentHash), and calculatePlanHash is deleted, not kept 'for display'. (h) exporter.ts csvCell() is the single CSV writer (formula neutralization, BOM, tombstones filtered); interop spreadsheet, the CLI and MCP all call it. (i) Delete the renderer.ts and reconciler.ts shims. Directory renames (controller.ts vs controller/, renderers/ vs rendering/) wait for a post-gate mechanical PR.
3. CANONICAL PLAYGROUND MODULES (duplicates and dead code). Delete: CloudBar.tsx and its 48 .cloud-bar CSS rules; UserHubModal.tsx; CloudRoomModal.tsx (its join-by-link/ID field moves into RoomPopover); the duplicate handleCreateRoom in useRoomSync; the unused command-bus events; the dead DTOs; every 'linked'/?url= source branch; useDynamicSync's stub fields. Adopt ModalContext, turned into a stack, in place of App's ~12 modal booleans, and move ReadOnlyFork, EditorLogin, Shortcuts and MonteCarlo into ModalHost. lib/identity.ts provides clientId (per browser, crypto.randomUUID) and tabId (per tab, in memory) and replaces the four copied peer-id getters. lib/ids.ts newId(prefix) replaces Date.now base36 ids in core and playground. One 128-bit generateRoomId replaces both generateRoomSlug copies, and normalizeUsername lives only in core. lib/download.ts downloadBlob (revokes the URL on the next tick) replaces four copies; one forkPlan() replaces three fork paths; one activateRoom() replaces seven or eight copy-pasted activation blocks. One pure filterTasks(tasks, criteria) replaces TaskQueryPipeline, its four stage classes and the divergent filters in TasksView, useDateFilter and useTaskActions. meta.ownerUid is the only definition of owner. schema/jantt.schema.json is canonical, apps/playground/public/schema/v1.json is copied at build, and a test checks that schema, types and examples agree.
4. APP.TSX SPLIT (1,073 lines; ARCH-26/PGSHELL-18/PGSTATE-18/PGVIEWS-05). Target: App.tsx at most 150 lines with no business logic. state/planStore.ts is a small typed external store on useSyncExternalStore (no new dependency) holding activeProjectId, data, role/readOnly, dirty and saveStatus, read through selector hooks, so the autosave ticker or a keystroke no longer re-renders the shell. state/commit.ts commitPlan(next, {origin}) is the single write gateway for Gantt, Canvas, Kanban, Tasks, Notes, the JSON editor, People/Teams and version restore. It enforces read-only, stamps fields through core stampTaskChanges, pushes an inverse patch onto the per-plan undo stack, and marks autosave and cloud dirty. The guard-less handleChartCommit path is deleted. Extracted hooks: useGlobalShortcuts (keymap registry), useLaunchParams (over urlState), useShareLinkImport, cloud/useCloudHub (owned/shared lists plus room actions); lib/exportActions.ts holds the exports. AppShell.tsx is layout only. ModalHost and ViewRouter props are fully typed (no any), and App.tsx stops re-exporting types and utils. Ceiling: no playground file over 400 lines, so PlanManagerModal (1,393) and ShareRoomModal (959) split into list, card and dialog components.
5. USEROOMSYNC SPLIT (1,044 lines; ARCH-27). firebase/roomRepository.ts is the only room I/O. Its typed methods (getMeta, watchMeta, watchData, watchMembers, commit(roomId, baseRevision, pathUpdates), create, delete, join, leave, requestAccess, connectPresence) return a typed SyncError with kind permission|offline|conflict|invalid|quota|unknown, and firebase/decoders.ts validates every snapshot. sync/roomSyncEngine.ts is a framework-free state machine: idle -> dirty -> saving -> (conflict -> merging -> saving), plus offline and error states. It debounces at 800 ms with a 5 s max-wait and keeps one in-flight commit plus one queued follow-up, so no edit is dropped. flush() runs on room switch, visibilitychange=hidden and pagehide. The server-acknowledged base is persisted per room as SavedProject.synced = {revision, data}, never taken from the autosave copy. hooks/useRoomSession(roomId) is the React binding and exposes status, role, lastSyncedAt, conflicts and flush. hooks/useRoomPresence(roomId) and cloud/roomActions.ts complete the split, and URL invite handling moves to useLaunchParams. The engine is unit-tested against an in-memory fake repository.
6. RTDB DATA MODEL AND PII. /users/$uid becomes private (read and write only by that user): {username, displayName<=80, photoURL https<=300, createdAt}. email, githubVerified and isDevBypass are removed; email stays only in Firebase Auth. /user_directory/$uid {username, displayName, photoURL} is readable by signed-in users only through `query.orderByChild == 'username' && query.limitToFirst <= 10`, has .indexOn username, and is written by the user in the same multi-path update as the username claim. /usernames/$name -> uid: claimable only when free, one per uid (newData users/$uid/username must equal $name), released on rename, matching ^[a-z0-9-]{3,39}$ (which fixes RULES-25). It is documented as a Jantt handle, not proof of the GitHub login, because rules cannot see the login. /user_rooms/$uid/{owned,shared}/$roomId = {addedAt} only, dropping the stale denormalized title and counts; the Plan Manager reads meta live. owned is validated against rooms/$roomId/meta/ownerUid. shared is writable by the user or the room owner, and only when members/$uid exists in newData. /rooms/$roomId = {meta, members, banned, access_requests, teams, data}. Presence moves to /presence/$roomId/$uid/$connId, with per-connection onDisconnect, which fixes multi-tab presence. meta = {title<=120, ownerUid (immutable), visibility 'private'|'link', schemaVersion, createdAt, updatedAt, revision, contentHash, taskCount, noteCount, theme (enum)}. No secretKey exists anywhere. Every node gets typed, length-capped .validate rules and "$other": {".validate": false}. $roomId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$, and every write requires auth.token.firebase.sign_in_provider == 'github.com'.
7. RTDB RULES MODEL (access). Helpers: O = meta/ownerUid == auth.uid; M = members/auth.uid exists; E = member role is editor; L = meta/visibility == 'link'; B = banned/auth.uid exists. Reads: meta, data and presence allow L||M||O; members and teams allow M||O; banned allows O; access_requests allows O, plus a user's own request. Writes: a room is created only when !data.exists(), newData meta/ownerUid == auth.uid and $roomId matches the pattern. Only O may delete a room. In meta, title/visibility/theme are writable by O; editors may write only the sync leaves (revision, contentHash, updatedAt, counts). data is writable by O||E, and only in a multi-path update that bumps meta/revision by exactly 1 (`newData.parent().child('meta/revision').val() == data.parent().child('meta/revision').val() + 1`); this is the optimistic-concurrency CAS. Concurrent commits from the same base are rejected atomically, and the losing client re-merges and retries. members/$uid: O may write anything; a user may delete their own record (leave) or create one as viewer only when L && !B. role is an enum, and the key is the identity (no uid field), which fixes the forged-uid issue (RULES-08). banned is O-only, and removing a member writes it, so revocation sticks. access_requests/$uid: the user may create {at}, O may delete. presence: self only, only when L||M, with a validated shape and no isOwner field. Edit links and the secretKey are removed: editors are granted by the owner, by inviting a username or approving an access request. The rules stay in database.rules.json, are deployed only by CI after the emulator matrix passes, and firebase.json gets an emulator config.
8. SYNC/MERGE MODEL, STATED HONESTLY. RTDB rooms are not a CRDT. They use server-serialized optimistic concurrency: each commit carries baseRevision, the rules accept only revision+1, and a rejected commit re-merges and retries. The merge is a deterministic 3-way merge (base = last server-acknowledged snapshot, plus local and remote), per entity and per field. A side whose value equals the base loses. Per-field LWW applies only when both sides changed the same field since the base. It uses timestamps corrected by Firebase .info/serverTimeOffset, with clientId as the tiebreak (fixing clock skew, CORESYNC-14), and it never falls back to task-level updatedAt (CORESYNC-02). Set-like arrays such as assignees and tags merge as 3-way sets, so removals are honored. Meta, notes, people, teams, categories, calendars and documents use the same logic (CORESYNC-05). Deletes are tombstones stamped at delete time and garbage-collected by age (at least 30 days) below the acknowledged revision; the 50-item cap goes. Conflicts are shown as a non-blocking notice with details. Storage v2 stores tasks, notes, people and teams as maps keyed by encoded id plus an order field, so a commit is a multi-path update of the changed entities only. v1 array rooms are read as-is and converted on their first v2 commit. Rename crdt-hash.ts to content-hash.ts and remove the 'CRDT', 'commutative' and '100% roundtrip' claims. @jantt/yjs stays the real CRDT option: updatePlan diffs against a base and deletes removed keys, it carries every section, seeding waits for provider sync, and remote data passes through sanitizePlan.
9. TRUST BOUNDARIES. Core sanitizePlan(untrusted, {source}) -> {plan, issues} is the single entry point for every untrusted plan: JSON editor, file import, #data= link, RTDB snapshot, Yjs, elements data-src, CLI file, MCP arguments and Python. It runs in O(n) once per inbound payload, never per render. It type-checks every field and drops __proto__/constructor/prototype keys (maps use Object.create(null)). It coerces colors to a strict CSS color grammar (hex, rgb(), hsl(), named; no url() or ';'), dates to ISO yyyy-mm-dd and numbers to finite values, caps string lengths, renames duplicate ids with a warning, and caps plan size (5,000 tasks / 2 MB encoded) and timeline span (30 years). Renderers still escape every interpolation and set styles only through validated element.style.setProperty. eslint-plugin-no-unsanitized bans innerHTML with interpolation, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML is banned in the playground. URL: lib/urlState.ts is the only reader and writer of location. Its keys are allowlisted (room, view, theme, scale, plan, data), each value is validated (roomId regex, enums), secrets never appear in a URL, and #data= is consumed once and then stripped with replaceState. Share payloads: at most 256 KB compressed, inflation aborted at 5 MB, sync metadata stripped, always imported as a new plan '<name> (imported)' behind a preview banner, never replacing a plan by name. A CSP meta tag sets script-src 'self'; connect-src to the Firebase hosts only; img-src 'self' https: data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'. Avatars load only from allowlisted https hosts, otherwise initials. CLI: binds to 127.0.0.1, uses a per-session token, checks Host and Origin, sends no CORS headers, and escapes JSON-in-HTML (</script>, U+2028). Python: JSON escaped for <script>, html.escape on title and theme. Worker: /api/room deleted; the proxy is limited to https on allowlisted hosts, with a size cap, a forced JSON/text content-type and Vary: Origin.
10. ERROR HANDLING AND LOGGING (ARCH-31, PGSHELL-06). Three React ErrorBoundary layers. Root fallback: Reload, Download all plans as JSON straight from storage, Reset UI state, Open template. Per view, keyed by view and plan: 'This view failed' with Switch view and Copy details. Per modal: the modal closes and a toast appears. lib/errors.ts reportError(err, {context, userMessage, severity}) routes errors to a toast (user-facing), the console (dev) and an optional telemetry sink that is off by default and scrubs PII and plan content. Typed errors: SyncError kinds, StorageQuotaError, and ImportError with a field path. Storage writes return a Result, so autosave never reports 'Saved' after a failed write. Core: JanttOptions.onError receives engine, handler and diagnostic errors (cycles, invalid data, duplicate ids); the engine never throws from DOM event handlers, and resolve returns diagnostics. Every network and RTDB operation gets a timeout (AbortSignal.timeout) and offline awareness through .info/connected. ESLint no-empty runs with allowEmptyCatch: false, so each of the 65 empty catches is either handled or carries an '// intentionally ignored: <reason>' comment. window error and unhandledrejection events are hooked into reportError.
11. SCHEDULING CONVENTION (CORESCHED-02/04/08/13, CORERENDER-17). Adopt MS Project/P6 semantics everywhere. End dates are inclusive and duration = end - start + 1 (in calendar or working days per the plan calendar). A task is a milestone only when milestone:true, so a single-day task is a bar. Links are FS/SS/FF/SF with a lag; FS+0 means the successor starts on the next working day. A missing lag gives FS meta.defaultGapDays and the other types 0; an explicit 0 is respected. The CPM and the cascade share one constraint function, so the highlighted critical path always matches the drawn schedule, and layout, the leveler, EVM and Monte Carlo pass the plan's gap and calendar. Working calendars (meta.calendar, useWorkingDays, data.calendars) reach resolve, the CPM, gestures, the leveler and Monte Carlo, with memoized holiday sets. Relaxation is one pass in topological order, O(V+E), replacing the 24 relaxation passes. Cycles are never cascaded: tasks in a cycle keep their dates and get a diagnostic, and the gesture and sidebar refuse links that would create one. A plan meta.schemaVersion bump migrates stored lags and gaps on load so no existing plan's dates move; golden tests over examples/ prove zero drift. Holidays: fix UK substitute days and US observed New Year (ISSUES-01). CA and AU leave the advertised list until they are implemented.
12. FALSE LOGIC TO MAKE REAL. Critical path: core CPM in Gantt and Canvas, replacing the canvas 'urgent tasks' toggle. Monte Carlo: Beta-PERT with lambda=4; honors scheduled starts; completed tasks are fixed and in-progress tasks sample only their remaining work; typed links and lags via the shared graph; criticality sorted for 'Top drivers'; runs in a real module Web Worker shipped as @jantt/core/worker-entry, with progress, cancel and a seed; inputs capped. EVM: PV from the active baseline, labelled 'no baseline' when it falls back. A missing actualCost gives AC 'n/a' instead of AC = EV. Plans without costs report clearly labelled schedule-only metrics instead of SPI 1.0. EAC and TCPI use the proper formulas. A baseline freeze stores estimatedCost as the budget, and its test is fixed. The S-curve shows the real PV curve and EV/AC points from snapshot history only, with currency via Intl.NumberFormat(meta.currency). Leveler: lowest priority deferred first; completed and in-progress tasks never move; calendars respected; one unresolvable conflict no longer aborts the other resources. Undo/redo: per-plan stacks of inverse field patches covering every commit path, cleared on plan switch, editors only. Autosave 'Manual only' is honored, with an unsaved-changes guard. Cross-tab sync: per-project keys, a storage event and a BroadcastChannel keyed by tabId. Version restore confirms and takes a pre-restore snapshot, which makes 'zero data loss' true for restores. Cloud sync status is shown. Team sharing resolves people with linked usernames to real uids, and unlinked people are listed as 'not on Jantt'. Room revocation works through the banned list. CLI live sync uses fs.watch plus a revision, and a stale save gets 409 and a reload prompt. Read-only is enforced in core controller public methods and dependency-line deletion. Kanban gets a Blocked column, and Todo status keeps progress consistent. Python from_dataframe honors its column parameters. <jantt-timeline> honors show-critical-path and show-baselines.
13. FALSE LOGIC TO RELABEL OR REMOVE. 'CRDT/commutative/100% roundtrip' becomes '3-way merge' in docs and comments. 'DCMA 14-point audit' becomes 'Schedule health (DCMA-inspired)', listing the checks it actually runs: the existing ones are corrected and the score is normalized by task count. The core worker.ts 'inline Blob off-main-thread' claim is removed and replaced by the real worker entry. The Notes 'Preview Markdown' toggle is removed until a safe React-element renderer exists. 'Lossless' MS Project/P6 interop becomes 'best-effort', with a table of preserved fields. 'Zero runtime dependencies' and '<14 KB' are replaced by the measured size-limit number (fflate is a dependency). 'PDF export' is removed from the CLI and README. exportSvgString is documented as a dependency-overlay SVG. The serverless REST rooms (/plans) and the worker /api/room are deleted. The GitHub-star verification gate is deleted (about 1.2k lines): it is client-only and unenforceable because its flags are self-writable, and the GitHub OAuth token is no longer persisted. Server-side enforcement would come back only as a Cloud Function claim. The 'Benchmark 10,000 tasks' button becomes dev-only (import.meta.env.DEV) and runs on a scratch plan, never the user's plan. The PERT 'made-up 95%' becomes 'n/a' when there is no target date. The Shortcuts sheet and palette are generated from the keymap registry. The security.md matrix, README and SECURITY.md are rewritten to match the deployed rules.
14. LOCAL PERSISTENCE (PGSTATE-05/06/19/29, ARCH-13). Storage v2 is an index key plus one key per project (jantt_project_<id>), with read-modify-write of a single entry so tabs no longer clobber each other's lists. Each project holds its own draft, so the shared ACTIVE_JSON slot is removed. Writes flush on plan switch, visibilitychange=hidden and pagehide, not only beforeunload, and the debounce has a max-wait so continuous typing cannot starve it. Quota errors surface with Free space (prune the oldest snapshots across the vault) and Export actions. The snapshot vault is per project with a total byte budget (about 2 MB, LRU) and deduplicates by contentHash. Unparseable entries are moved to quarantine and offered under 'Recover' in the Plan Manager instead of being silently discarded. The schema is versioned and migrated from v1 on first load, with the legacy key kept untouched for one release. All of the 69 raw localStorage calls go through storageService, except a short lint-allowed list for feature detection.
15. PUBLIC API, PACKAGING, VERSIONING. All @jantt/* packages release in lockstep as 2.0.0. The breaking changes: firebase-sync removed; remote-sync moved to a subpath with no default proxy; detail-modal removed; explicit exports. Core CSS exports point to files Vite 8 actually emits, and a test resolves every package.json export and README import path after build (fixing COREINTERACT-37, BINDINGS-18/19 and ISSUES-02). Standalone's style field points to dist/standalone.css. React, Vue, Svelte and Yjs take @jantt/core as a peerDependency. The React bundle gets 'use client', and @jantt/elements is SSR-safe, upgrades properties set before definition and patches instead of remounting. The root package.json is the single version source, injected at build as __JANTT_VERSION__ into Jantt.version, standalone, the CLI and MCP; the release script updates Python's version and CDN pin. Changesets generate the CHANGELOG, and 1.x gets a deprecation notice that points to a migration guide.
16. DEPENDENCY TARGETS. Node: drop 20 (EOL since April 2026). Set engines to >=22.12.0 everywhere with engine-strict in .npmrc, .nvmrc 24, a CI matrix of 22.x and 24.x, and Docker node:24-alpine (multi-stage, .dockerignore, nginx with gzip/brotli plus security and cache headers). vitest moves to the major whose peer range includes Vite 8 (^5.1 per ISSUES-04), hoisted to the root with one workspace config, so only one Vite is in the lockfile. jsdom is unified at ^29 in the root. vite stays ^8; vite-plugin-dts goes to the latest major; TypeScript goes to the latest stable with strict in every package. firebase goes to the latest 12.x, lazy-loaded. lucide-react goes to the latest 0.x, capped at <1 per the owner's revert. The playground stays on React 18.3 this cycle, and bindings declare a react peer range of ^18.2 || ^19. New runtime dependencies, playground only: @floating-ui/dom for placement, and @dnd-kit/core plus @dnd-kit/sortable for accessible drag and drop on mouse, touch and keyboard. New dev dependencies: ESLint 9 flat config with typescript-eslint, react-hooks, jsx-a11y and no-unsanitized; knip for dead exports; size-limit; fast-check; @testing-library/react; @playwright/test with @axe-core/playwright; firebase-tools with @firebase/rules-unit-testing; changesets. Python: requires-python >=3.10, CI on 3.10 through 3.14, pandas and polars extras tested and included in [all]. The owner's removal of Dependabot stands: no version-bump bot. Instead, npm audit --audit-level=high gates CI and a weekly scheduled audit opens one issue.
17. TESTING STRATEGY. Core unit tests: golden schedules over examples/ (zero date drift); graph and cycle cases; typed links, zero lag and calendars; a property that the CPM critical chain equals the cascade's driving chain. Analytics numeric tests: seeded 20k-sample Beta-PERT mean and SD within tolerance; EVM cases for no costs, CPI 0 and baselines; leveler cases for capacity >1, priorities, done tasks and tombstones. Reconciler property-based tests (fast-check) under server serialization: convergence, idempotence, no resurrected deletes. A type-level test checks that TASK_SYNC_FIELDS covers every key of Task, and a test checks that changing any synced field changes contentHash. Security: one shared hostile-plan fixture (script and img payloads in labels, colors, dates and costs; url() colors; __proto__ keys; an oversized payload) runs against every sink: grid, tooltip, sidebar, palette, notes, canvas, report, CLI HTML and Python to_html. RTDB rules: @firebase/rules-unit-testing on the Database emulator with a matrix of {anon, stranger, viewer, editor, owner, banned} x every path x read/create/update/delete. It also covers the revision-CAS race, /users privacy, directory query limits and username uniqueness. It is a required CI job, and rules deploy only from CI. Playground: vitest plus Testing Library for roomSyncEngine with a fake repository (offline, conflict, edits during in-flight saves, flush on switch), storage v2 migration and quota, urlState, undo scoping, and the Modal primitive (focus trap and return, Escape, backdrop rule). The self-testing room-security-and-roles.test.ts is deleted. E2E: a Playwright smoke suite on the built app against the emulators covers create/edit/reload, Plan Manager moves by menu, drag and keyboard, RoomPopover flows, two-context live collaboration, a critical-path-plus-scroll screenshot of the sticky header, and an axe scan of every dialog, at desktop and mobile viewports. Tools: CLI spawn tests (token/origin, exit codes), MCP stdio protocol tests (ping, notifications, isError), and pytest for NaN/NaT and escaping. Clocks are injected with vi.setSystemTime, so no time bombs remain. Coverage floors: 80% lines for core scheduling/reconciliation and playground sync/storage, with no global percentage vanity target.
18. PERFORMANCE BUDGETS (CI-enforced where measurable). Core: a drag frame takes at most 8 ms at 1,000 tasks, because only the dragged bars and their links are patched and the full render happens on pointerup. Initial render: at most 100 ms for 1k tasks and 300 ms for 10k, with row and column virtualization from the existing virtualizer and keyed DOM reuse (persistent header, grid and SVG layers). resolve plus CPM for 5k tasks takes at most 30 ms. Wheel and slider are rAF-throttled and search is debounced at 150 ms. Critical-path styling is static, with no infinite box-shadow or filter animations. Timeline span is capped. Playground: initial JS at most 300 KB gzip, with Firebase, interop, render-canvas, Monte Carlo and cloud dialogs lazy-loaded, measured by size-limit. The shell does not re-render on ticks; relative times re-render locally. JSON editor parsing is debounced at 250 ms. Monte Carlo runs in a Worker, so no main-thread task exceeds 50 ms. The share URL is built only when the Share dialog opens. Sync: listeners cover meta and data, not the room root; commit payload grows with the changed entities; presence lives off the room node. The @jantt/core gzip budget is the measured baseline plus 5%. vitest bench runs in CI and blocks on a regression above 20%.
19. EXECUTION STRUCTURE. Phase 0 freezes the cross-cutting contracts as typed stubs with tests, so the parallel workstreams never block each other: sanitizePlan, contentHash, TASK_SYNC_FIELDS and stampTaskChanges, plan-ops, the graph API, date conventions, planStore and commitPlan, the roomRepository interface and SyncError, the Modal/Popover/Menu/ConfirmDialog props, the urlState API, and the rules model. Exclusive file ownership: WS-A core scheduling and analytics; WS-B core rendering, interaction, theme.css and escaping; WS-C core reconciliation plus playground sync/ and the useRoomSync replacement; WS-D database.rules.json, firebase/ services, the migration script and emulator tests; WS-E App, state, storage, urlState, undo, shortcuts and error boundaries; WS-F playground UI primitives, modals, Plan Manager, Navbar/RoomPopover and views; WS-G bindings, interop and render-canvas; WS-H CLI, MCP, Python and worker; WS-I build, CI, release, Docker and docs. WS-C and WS-D pair on the commit/CAS contract. Each workstream's review starts as soon as its coding ends, the global gate runs last, and nothing is committed before owner sign-off.

## 4. UX decisions (incl. owner requests in changes_required.md)

1. OWNER ASK 1: critical path painting over the sticky header (CORERENDER-01, PGSHELL-07). The fix is at the stacking-context level, not with bigger z-indexes. The chart body (gridContainer, which gets its missing class jantt-grid-container) becomes position:relative with isolation:isolate and z-index:0. Bars, links, the today line, critical styling and the lasso marquee can then never escape it. The sticky timeline header sits above the body, and the label column and corner sit above that, all on documented tokens. The z-index:14/15 !important rules on .is-critical are removed, and critical links are drawn last in SVG order. The infinite box-shadow/filter pulse becomes a static 2px outline that does not grow bars by 4px, with an optional one-shot highlight that is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. The Canvas view gets the same treatment: hit-testing ignores the header band. A Playwright screenshot test locks it: toggle the critical path, scroll 500px, and the header pixels must be unchanged.
2. OWNER ASK 2: the Plan Manager is exactly three lists: 'On this device', 'My cloud rooms' and 'Shared with me'. Cached room copies that have no pointer appear in the list they belong to with a 'cached' badge, and the built-in template moves to the New plan dialog. At 960px and wider the lists are three columns; below that, a select or segmented control (with counts) switches the single visible list. Each card shows title, last updated, task count and role badge, plus a 'Move to...' menu that offers only valid transfers with explicit verbs. Device to My cloud: 'Upload to cloud' (keeps the local copy) or 'Move to cloud' (removes the local copy only after the server acknowledges, with an Undo toast). My cloud to device: 'Save a copy on this device' (the room is untouched). Shared to device: 'Save a copy'. Shared to My cloud: 'Fork to my cloud'. Drag and drop (dnd-kit with mouse, touch and keyboard) calls the same transferPlan(item, target) with the non-destructive default verb. Invalid targets dim and explain why, and the global Move/Copy toggle is removed. A drop never deletes anything: Delete and Leave live only in the card menu, behind a ConfirmDialog. Signed-out users see a single sign-in CTA in the cloud lists instead of dead-end drop targets. Each card has its own busy state and transfers are single-flight, so no duplicate rooms. Search spans all three lists.
3. OWNER ASK 3: the cloud subheader moves into popovers. The Subheader row is deleted, which removes one 46px bar. The Navbar gets three anchored triggers. (a) PlanSwitcher, 'Plan name ▾': a popover with search, the three lists for quick switching, and New plan / Import file... / Manage plans.... Import lives here and in the Plan Manager. (b) RoomChip: a local plan shows 'On this device · Go live'; a room shows '● Live · Editor · 3 online', with the dot colored by sync status. It opens a 360px RoomPopover containing: the sync status line with Retry; your role and one primary CTA (Sign in to edit / Request edit access / Make a local copy); online avatars; Copy view link; Invite people (owner, opens Members & access); a visibility switch (owner: Private / Anyone with the link can view); Leave room / Delete room (destructive, confirmed); and, for local plans, Join by link or ID. (c) A People button with a count. On mobile the same content opens as bottom sheets from the action menu.
4. OWNER ASK 4a: one dialog system. The Modal is built on native <dialog>.showModal(). That puts it in the browser's top layer, which ends the z-index wars (1000/9999/10000/99999), makes the background inert, and means the mobile bottom nav can no longer cover footers. Sizes: sm 400, md 560 and lg 800px, max-height calc(100dvh - 32px), with fixed header and footer so only the body scrolls. Anatomy: an h2 title wired to aria-labelledby, an optional one-line description, and a close button with an aria-label. The footer is right-aligned: secondary (Cancel), then primary. Destructive actions use the danger style and verb-plus-object labels ('Delete room for 4 people'), are never focused by default, and always go through a ConfirmDialog that states the consequence and whether it can be undone. Behavior: focus moves to the first field (or the primary button) and returns to the trigger on close; Tab is trapped; Escape closes, but a dirty form asks 'Discard changes?'. A backdrop click closes only non-form dialogs, and only when both pointerdown and pointerup land on the backdrop, so text-selection drags no longer close dialogs. Scroll is locked with html:has(dialog[open]){overflow:hidden}. One modal is open at a time; the only stacking allowed is a ConfirmDialog on top. This replaces every window.confirm/alert and the 12 ad-hoc modal shells, and fixes the dead mobile CSS selectors.
5. OWNER ASK 4b: popovers and menus. Popover and Menu are built on the Popover API, which also uses the top layer, so they are never clipped by scrolling columns or overflow:hidden. @floating-ui/dom positions them: preferred placement bottom-start, flip and shift with an 8px viewport margin, size() caps max-height to the available space with internal scroll, and they reposition on scroll and resize. They are anchored to a trigger that carries aria-expanded and aria-controls. They close on outside click or Escape and return focus to the trigger. Menus use role=menu with arrow keys, Home/End and typeahead. This applies to the plan card menus (no more clipped, upward-only menu), RoomPopover, PlanSwitcher, the note color and attach pickers, and the mention list (which also closes on blur and caret moves). Core's toolbar Settings popover uses the same Popover API with a small built-in measure/flip/clamp in place of the hard-coded 260px, so it escapes the sticky header and label column (CORERENDER-02/03).
6. MOBILE. At 640px and below, every Modal and Popover renders as a bottom sheet with a drag handle, safe-area padding and a 100dvh cap. The bottom nav is inert while any sheet or dialog is open. One breakpoint set is shared by CSS and JS: a matchMedia hook replaces the UA heuristic, which also covers the gap between 769px and wide desktop. Immersive landscape keeps a compact nav instead of a lone 'Plans' button. The core task drawer's pull handle supports drag-to-dismiss. File import (JSON, XML, XER, CSV) works on mobile from the action menu, and toasts sit above the bottom nav.
7. KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS. One keymap registry drives the key handler, the Shortcuts sheet and the command palette, so nothing is advertised that does not exist. Single-key shortcuts fire only when no modifier is held, when focus is not in an input, select, textarea or contenteditable, and when no dialog or popover is open; Ctrl+C copies again. The standard set: Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the palette; Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z undo and redo (per plan, editors only); ? shows shortcuts; Escape closes the topmost layer, otherwise cancels an in-progress drag; Delete removes the focused task with an Undo toast; arrow keys nudge the focused bar and keep focus. The palette renders text only, never HTML.
8. STATUS, EMPTY, LOADING AND ERROR STATES. Save status is always truthful and specific: 'Saved on this device'; 'Not saved — storage full · Free space'; 'Saving to cloud...'; 'Offline — 3 changes queued'; 'Can't save — view only'. Opening a room shows a skeleton with 'Connecting...', which times out at 10s to 'Keep working offline / Retry'. Every view has an empty state whose single CTA does exactly what it says ('Clear all filters' clears every filter, not just the date filter), and a filtered list never claims there is no data. The per-view error fallback offers Copy details and Export plan JSON. Analytics show 'n/a — add costs' or 'n/a — set a baseline' instead of invented numbers, and currency is formatted correctly, including negatives and overspend.
9. TOASTS. A queue of at most three, bottom-center above the bottom nav with a safe-area offset, rendered in the top layer after any dialog so they are never hidden behind one. role=status, or role=alert for errors. Info toasts auto-dismiss after 5s; errors stay until dismissed. Each toast can carry one action (Undo / Retry / Reload) and has a dismiss button. One toast per user-visible event: there is no toast per remote snapshot (remote activity shows in the RoomChip), and remote updates never overwrite the JSON editor while the user is typing.
10. ROLES AND READ-ONLY. Viewers see disabled controls with a 'View only' tooltip and one persistent state in the RoomChip offering Request edit access / Make a local copy, instead of a fork prompt on every click. JSON stays selectable and copyable for viewers. Owner-only controls (invite, remove, visibility, delete) are hidden from non-owners rather than shown and then failing. Role badges (Owner / Editor / Viewer) are identical in Share, Members & access, Plan Manager and presence. Viewers cannot change task status from any view, and the core chart enforces read-only too, including dependency-line deletion. Opening a room no longer silently adds the user to its roster.
11. SHARING CLARITY. The Share dialog offers three clearly labelled choices. 'Snapshot link': a copy of the plan carried in the URL, no live updates, with its size shown and a warning when it is too long. 'Room link': live and view-only for anyone with the link, available only when visibility is 'link'. 'Invite people': owners add editors by username, and access requests are approved here. No link, embed snippet, WhatsApp share or native share ever contains a secret, and the address bar never does either. Exports (JSON, CSV, MS Project, P6, Executive report) live in one Export menu and produce identical files wherever it is opened. Every copy action awaits the clipboard and reports failure.
12. ACCESSIBILITY BASELINE: WCAG 2.2 AA. All controls are native buttons or links with accessible names, so no clickable divs. Kanban, Tasks and Notes lists use listbox or grid semantics with keyboard operation. Every drag and drop has the 'Move to...' alternative and dnd-kit live announcements; Kanban gets real drag and drop with the same keyboard support. A visible focus-ring token meets 3:1, text contrast is at least 4.5:1 in every theme (the critical-path toggle's active state is fixed), and prefers-reduced-motion is honored. Gantt bars use a roving tabindex and keep focus across re-renders thanks to keyed DOM patching; locks and milestones are keyboard-operable, and the table splitter is keyboard-resizable. The task sidebar is a labelled dialog with a focus trap, and Escape asks before discarding edits. The canvas view has an aria-label and a 'switch to accessible Gantt view' link. The collapsed JSON editor is inert. axe runs in CI on every dialog.
13. GANTT HEADER AND INTERACTION POLISH. The zoomed-out header renders week and quarter tiers with no overlapping labels, and the Year preset maps to its own tier. Escape cancels a drag, and pointercancel aborts instead of committing. Edge auto-scroll keeps the bar under the cursor. The 3px threshold also guards date changes at small zoom. Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zoom is proportional to deltaY and anchored at the cursor. The table splitter stays attached to the sticky label column. The default 'fit' row mode never hides tasks. Single-day tasks render as bars, not diamonds, and the grid and tooltip show the same duration.

## 5. Rollout & risk

- DAY-0 PII HOTFIX (needs owner sign-off out of band; it should not wait for the full cycle). First, back up the database with `firebase database:get / > backup-<date>.json`, stored offline and encrypted and deleted after 30 days. Then deploy a minimal rules change that removes the `.read: true` on /users and makes /users/$uid readable only by that user. Then run an admin script that deletes email, githubVerified and isDevBypass from every /users record. Known side effect: teammate search in the current client returns nothing until the /user_directory client ships, which is acceptable against a live email leak. Because every account's email was publicly retrievable, the owner should check whether this is a notifiable personal-data breach (for example GDPR Art. 33/34) and record the assessment.
- RULES VS CLIENT ORDER. Rules are server-enforced and hit every deployed tab at once, so the order is compatibility-first. (1) Release client N+1, which works under both rule sets. It reads meta and data separately, writes presence to /presence, commits through the data-node CAS, maintains /user_directory, never writes secretKey or email, and maps PERMISSION_DENIED to a 'Reload to update' banner. It also checks a new /config/minClientVersion node at startup (public read, admin write). (2) Run the RTDB migration. (3) Deploy the new rules from CI, only after the emulator matrix passes. (4) Bump minClientVersion so stale tabs reload. (5) Remove the compatibility shims in N+2. Rules rollback means redeploying the previous rules JSON from git; the migration only adds or removes data that the old rules never relied on, so a rollback cannot strand migrated data.
- RTDB DATA MIGRATION. A firebase-admin script that the owner runs locally with a service account. It has a dry-run mode that prints a diff, it is idempotent and resumable per room, and it runs only after a fresh backup. Users: strip PII, build /user_directory, validate usernames, and report collisions or invalid handles for manual resolution rather than resolving them automatically. Rooms: set meta.visibility='link', which preserves today's behavior where every room is readable by link (owners can then switch to Private); set meta.schemaVersion; delete meta.secretKey; drop rooms/*/presence; remove fabricated team member uids that have no /users record; normalize members to {role, username, displayName, photoURL, addedAt}. user_rooms: drop orphan pointers and denormalized fields. Room data stays in v1 arrays and converts lazily to keyed maps on its first v2 commit. During the transition window the rules accept both shapes; afterwards only v2. A verification script checks counts and spot-checks rooms afterwards.
- LOCAL DATA MIGRATION. On first load the new client migrates storage v1 (one monolithic project list plus the ACTIVE_JSON slot) to per-project keys and keeps the legacy key untouched as a backup for one release. Unparseable entries are quarantined and offered under 'Recover', never discarded. Plans are migrated to the new scheduling convention under meta.schemaVersion, and golden tests over examples/ prove zero date drift. The snapshot vault is pruned to its byte budget only after migration succeeds. Old share links (#data=) still decode, but now always import as a new plan.
- FEATURE FLAGS AND ENVIRONMENTS. Flags are build-time VITE_FF_* values with a localStorage override for dogfooding; there are no URL flags. They are ff.syncV2 (the new sync engine), ff.shellV2 (Navbar chips, RoomPopover, the new Plan Manager and the dialog system) and ff.storageV2. Add a separate staging Firebase project and a Pages preview: flags are on in staging and switched on in production after a soak, and each flag is deleted one release after GA. Rules changes cannot be flagged, which is why the compatibility-first order above exists. The emulators are used in dev and CI; production builds fail if the VITE_FIREBASE_* variables are missing, and the hard-coded production fallback is removed.
- MONITORING AND ABUSE CONTROL. reportError feeds counters for sync errors by kind, permission-denied by path, quota errors, conflict rate, commit retries and error-boundary crashes. The sink is an opt-in telemetry service with PII and plan content scrubbed, or console-only if the owner prefers no third party. Set Firebase console alerts on bandwidth, concurrent connections, storage and a billing budget. Run App Check (reCAPTCHA Enterprise) in monitor mode for two weeks, then enforce it on RTDB; this stands in for per-user quotas, which rules alone cannot express. A weekly npm audit job runs. Pages deploys only after CI is green (tests, typecheck, e2e) and never cancels an in-flight production deploy.
- PACKAGE RELEASE. All @jantt/* packages release in lockstep as 2.0.0 through changesets with npm provenance. The release workflow checks tag == version and runs build, typecheck and tests before publishing. It packs every package first and then publishes all of them or none, using a least-privilege token and SHA-pinned actions. A migration guide covers the removed APIs (firebase-sync, the default remote proxy, detail-modal, export *) and the corrected CSS paths. The latest 1.x gets a deprecation notice. The release script updates the Python package version and its CDN pin. The Docker image is rebuilt and smoke-tested in CI.
- EXECUTION RISKS AND CUT LINE. The biggest delivery risks are WS-C (sync engine) and WS-D (rules); they share the commit/CAS contract and the emulator matrix and must pair on both. Phase-0 contract freezing keeps the other seven workstreams unblocked, and the mechanical core directory renames are deferred to a post-gate PR. If the cycle has to be time-boxed, the cut line is: ship every security, data-loss and false-logic correctness fix plus the four owner UX asks; defer full DOM virtualization beyond the drag fast path, interop fidelity improvements, and the low-severity docs and consistency items. Nothing is committed before the owner signs off on the global gate.

## 6. Execution model

1. **Code (parallel):** each workstream below owns an exclusive set of files, so all of them run at the same time in one working tree. Package manifests, lockfile, tsconfig and Vite configs belong only to `buildci`.
2. **Per-workstream review (pipelined):** the moment a workstream's coding finishes, an adversarial reviewer re-reads its diff, fixes defects, and runs that package's typecheck/tests.
3. **Cross-cutting pass:** XSS/URL-hardening (`XSS-*`) and architecture (`ARCH-*`) findings span many files; they are routed to the owning workstream's files after the first pass.
4. **Final gate:** regenerate the lockfile, then `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:python`, plus a final whole-diff review.
5. **Principles:** smallest robust change; no new abstraction without two real callers; no hot-path perf regressions; backward-compatible public APIs unless a decision above says otherwise.

## 8. Workstreams

## WS-01 · Firebase RTDB security rules & DTO contracts  (`rules`)

- **Goal:** Make `database.rules.json` the single, emulator-tested enforcement layer for every RTDB path, so no PII is exposed, no role can be escalated and every node has a validated shape. Make the DTOs the exact mirror of that wire contract, validated on read.
- **Owned files (exclusive):**
  - `database.rules.json`
  - `firebase.json`
  - `database.rules.test.md` (new: rules test matrix)
  - `apps/playground/src/firebase/rules.test.ts` (new)
  - `apps/playground/src/firebase/types.ts`
  - `apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/index.ts`
  - `apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/UserDto.ts`
  - `apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/RoomDto.ts`
  - `apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/PresenceDto.ts`
  - `apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/RtdbCodec.ts`
  - `apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/TransactionDto.ts` (delete)
  - `packages/core/tests/room-security-and-roles.test.ts` (delete)
  - `packages/core/tests/rtdb-codec.test.ts`
  - `docs/security.md`
  - `SECURITY.md`
- **Contracts:** None are given in the plan metadata. This workstream **publishes** the RTDB wire contract: the paths, shapes and limits table and the frozen DTO exports, both in Notes. `fbsvc` (services), `roomsync` (sync and Share UI) and `coresync` (codec and hash) code against it in parallel, so the DTO export names are frozen on day 0, before any rule is written.
- **Exit criteria:**
  - `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` are green, with every `fbsvc`/`roomsync` consumer compiling against the new DTO exports. `git grep -nE "TransactionDto|isPublic|isOwner|\.email\b|secretKey" apps/playground/src` returns only the legacy `meta/secretKey` delete in `fbsvc`.
  - `npm test` runs the **static** block of `apps/playground/src/firebase/rules.test.ts` and it passes. That block covers rules↔DTO-limits↔docs lockstep and the DTO parsers. The emulator block skips cleanly when no emulator is running.
  - `npm run test:rules -w @jantt/playground` (Database emulator, project `demo-jantt`) passes every row of `database.rules.test.md`, locally and in the CI `rules` job.
  - `packages/core/tests/rtdb-codec.test.ts` passes, including the new RTDB-normalization roundtrip and hash-stability cases. This needs the `coresync` codec change.
  - Against the emulator:
    - Anonymous `GET /users.json`, `/public_profiles.json`, `/usernames.json` and `/plans/x.json` are denied.
    - An editor cannot change `members`, `teams` or `meta/ownerUid`, and cannot delete `data`.
    - A non-member cannot write presence.
    - An anonymous read of a `link` room succeeds; the same read of a `members` room is denied.
  - The §7 matrix in `docs/security.md` lists exactly the rule paths (checked by the lockstep test), and `SECURITY.md` names the Firebase backend as in scope.

### Tasks (severity order)

#### [ ] RULES-02 · /users is publicly readable and stores every account's email (full PII directory dump)  `critical` `security` `effort M`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:3-5, apps/playground/src/firebase/authService.ts:88, :238, apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/UserDto.ts:8, apps/playground/src/components/cloud/ShareRoomModal.tsx:639, :672
- **Problem:** `users` has `.read: true` plus `.indexOn: ["username"]`, and every profile is written with `email: user.email || ""`. An unauthenticated `GET <db>/users.json` therefore dumps every uid, email, display name and GitHub handle. Signed-in users also see other users' emails in Share search results.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules:
    - `users/$uid` `.read` and `.write` are `auth.uid === $uid` only. Remove the parent `.read` and `.indexOn`.
    - Add the directory `public_profiles/$uid` `{uid, username, displayUsername, displayName, photoURL?, updatedAt}`. A signed-in GitHub user may list it only via `query.orderByChild === 'username' && query.limitToFirst != null && query.limitToFirst <= 20`. Add `.indexOn: ["username"]`, self-write and `$other: false`.
    - No node accepts `email`: `$other: false` on `users/$uid` rejects it.
  - DTO:
    - Remove `email` from `UserProfile`.
    - Add `PublicProfile`, `toPublicProfile(profile)` and `parsePublicProfile(key, raw)` (uid := snapshot key) to `UserDto.ts`.
  - Client → `fbsvc`:
    - `signInWithGitHub` and `claimUsername` write `users/<uid>` and `usernames/<u>` in one multi-path update, using full-node values so legacy `email` and verification fields are dropped at next sign-in. This is the lazy migration.
    - Write `public_profiles/<uid>` right after. It is idempotent and re-synced on every sign-in, so the client works under both old and new rules during rollout.
    - `searchUsersByUsername` queries `public_profiles`.
  - Client → `roomsync`: remove `{user.email}` and `{selectedUser.email}` from `ShareRoomModal`; show `@username` plus displayName.
- **Verify:** `rules.test.ts`:
  - Denied: anon or other-user `get(users/<uid>)`, an unbounded `get(public_profiles)`, and `set(users/<me>/email, "x")`.
  - Allowed: `query(public_profiles, orderByChild('username'), startAt('ab'), endAt('ab'), limitToFirst(8))`.
  - Manual: `curl <db>/users.json` returns `Permission denied`.

#### [ ] RULES-03 · Editor branch of the room .write compares non-leaf val() values: editors either can rewrite members/teams or cannot save at all  `high` `rules-security` `effort M`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:32, apps/playground/src/firebase/roomService.ts:449, :462
- **Problem:** The editor clause of `rooms/$roomId/.write` checks `newData.child('members').val() === data.child('members').val()`. `val()` on a node with children does not compare content, so the check is meaningless. Either editors can rewrite the roster in one transaction (self → `owner`, delete the owner record, add accomplices, create teams), or every editor save is `PERMISSION_DENIED`. `saveRoomDataAtomic` transacts on `rooms/$id`, which only this branch authorizes for editors, so commit 52ec345 does not do what it claims.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules:
    - `$roomId/.write` allows only create (`!data.exists() && newData.child('meta/ownerUid').val() === auth.uid`) or owner (`data.child('meta/ownerUid').val() === auth.uid`). Delete the editor clause.
    - Editors get write only at `data` (`members/<auth.uid>/role === 'editor' && newData.exists()`, so an editor cannot delete the plan) and at the meta leaves listed in RULES-15/RULES-20.
    - `$roomId/.validate` keeps `members/<meta.ownerUid>` present.
  - Client → `fbsvc`: save = `runTransaction(rooms/${id}/data)` followed by one `update(rooms/${id}/meta, …)` (RULES-20).
- **Verify:** `rules.test.ts` "editor cannot …":
  - Denied: `set(members/<self>/role,'owner')`, `update(rooms/R,{members:…})`, `set(teams/t1,…)`, `set(meta/ownerUid,<self>)`, `remove(data)`, and any `runTransaction(rooms/R)`.
  - Allowed: `runTransaction(rooms/R/data)`.

#### [ ] RULES-05 · Signed-out create/save path writes to /plans via unauthenticated REST, which the rules default-deny  `high` `false-logic` `effort S`
- **Where:** packages/core/src/firebase-sync.ts:242-251, :340, :365-394, apps/playground/src/hooks/useRoomSync.ts:263-304, :379, :542-636, :961-1003
- **Problem:** Signed-out create and save send `PUT ${baseUrl}/plans/${roomId}.json` with no token. The rules have no `plans` node, so RTDB default-denies the request (401). `saveCloudRoom` also runs `sanitizeRoomId` (`room_ab12` → `room-ab12`) and targets `plans/` while the room was read from `rooms/`. As a result, signed-out room creation always fails, and `#key=` holders are labelled "Collaborator (Live Sync)" while every autosave fails.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules: keep `/plans` default-deny deliberately (add no node). Document "cloud editing requires GitHub sign-in" in `docs/security.md`.
  - Client → `roomsync`: delete the serverless branches in `useRoomSync` (`createCloudRoom` 263-304 and 961-1003, `saveCloudRoom` 542-636). Signed-out link holders get read-only mode plus a "Sign in to edit" CTA.
  - Core → `coresync` (same defect as CORESYNC-20/21/22/24/25): remove the `/plans` REST helpers in `firebase-sync.ts`. If they must stay exported for semver, keep them as deprecated stubs that throw a clear error; coordinate the export list with `coreinteract`.
- **Verify:**
  - `rules.test.ts`: anon and `gh(uid)` `set(plans/x,{})` are denied. This guards against "fixing" it with a permissive node.
  - Manual: signed out, open a room link → read-only banner with a Sign-in CTA, and no network PUT to `/plans`.

#### [ ] RULES-06 · Usernames can be squatted without limit and are not bound to the caller's GitHub login  `high` `rules-security` `effort M`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:10-14, apps/playground/src/firebase/authService.ts:102-105, apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/UserDto.ts:50-56, apps/playground/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:142-162
- **Problem:**
  - `usernames/$u` only checks first claim and `newData.val() === auth.uid`. There is no format check, no one-per-uid limit, no link to `users/$uid/username` and no release, so one account can script-claim thousands of handles.
  - A squatted handle makes the victim's first-sign-in multi-path update fail. `loginWithGitHub` has no catch, so the error is unhandled.
  - `normalizeUsername` strips `-`, so the logins `foo-bar` and `foobar` collide.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules, `usernames/$u`:
    - `.read`: signed-in GitHub user, per key only (no parent read, so no listing).
    - `.write` claim: `!data.exists()`.
    - `.write` release: `data.val() === auth.uid && !newData.exists()`, only when the same update moves `users/<uid>/username` off `$u`.
    - `.validate`: `$u.matches(/^[a-z0-9_-]{1,39}$/) && newData.val() === auth.uid`. In addition, `newData` root `users/<auth.uid>/username === $u`, and the previous name (`root.child('users/'+auth.uid+'/username')`) must be released in the same update. This gives exactly one live claim per uid; a rename is one multi-path update.
    - `users/$uid/.write` additionally requires `newData.exists() || !newData.parent().parent().child('usernames/'+data.child('username').val()).exists()`. Without it, delete-profile-then-reclaim loops around the one-claim limit.
  - DTO:
    - Add `USERNAME_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9_-]{1,39}$/`.
    - `normalizeUsername` becomes a re-export of `@jantt/core`, which keeps `-`. `coresync` changes `firebase-sync.ts:118` and the `firebase-sync.test.ts:56` expectation.
    - Stored usernames are not renamed.
  - Client → `fbsvc`:
    - In `signInWithGitHub`, catch `PERMISSION_DENIED` on the claim and route to `UsernameOnboardingModal` with "@handle is already claimed".
    - `useAuth.loginWithGitHub` catches the error and surfaces it.
  - Residual risk (documented, not built): binding a name to the caller's GitHub **login** needs a trusted server, because the ID token only carries the numeric GitHub id. The provider check (RULES-18) plus one name per uid caps squatting at one name per GitHub account.
- **Verify:** `rules.test.ts`:
  - Denied: a second claim while the first is still held; keys `Foo`, `a.b` and a 40-character name; release by another uid; claiming a taken name; deleting `users/<me>` while `usernames/<mine>` still exists.
  - Allowed: rename A→B in one update that includes `usernames/A: null`.

#### [ ] RULES-07 · /users/$uid has no .validate: users can set any username/uid on their profile and impersonate others in search  `high` `rules-security` `effort S`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:6-8, apps/playground/src/firebase/authService.ts:268-283, apps/playground/src/components/cloud/ShareRoomModal.tsx:176
- **Problem:** `users/$uid` is self-writable with no `.validate`. A user can set `username` to anyone's handle without owning the claim, forge `uid`, and add arbitrary large fields. `searchUsersByUsername` returns `child.val()` and Share uses the body's `selectedUser.uid`. The owner can therefore grant editor to an impostor, or to an arbitrary third party through a forged uid.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules, on `users/$uid` and `public_profiles/$uid`:
    - `.validate: newData.hasChildren(['uid','username','displayName','createdAt'])`.
    - `uid === $uid`.
    - `username` must be claimed by `$uid` in newData: `newData.parent().parent().parent().child('usernames/'+newData.val()).val() === $uid`. This also works for same-update claims.
    - Caps: `displayName` and `displayUsername` ≤256, `photoURL` `https://` and ≤1024, dates as strings ≤40.
    - `$other: false`.
  - DTO: `parsePublicProfile(key, raw)` forces `uid = key` and drops entries that fail `validateUsername` or have non-string fields.
  - Client → `fbsvc`: `searchUsersByUsername` maps results through `parsePublicProfile` (uid comes from `child.key`).
  - Client → `roomsync`: `ShareRoomModal` passes only that uid.
- **Verify:**
  - `rules.test.ts`: denied for `set(users/<me>/username,'victim')` when the victim holds the claim, for `uid: <other>`, and for an extra field `foo`. Allowed for the same-update claim plus profile.
  - Static block: `parsePublicProfile('u1',{uid:'u2',…}).uid === 'u1'`.

#### [ ] RULES-21 · Team sharing is non-functional: phantom uids never match accounts and undefined avatar/color makes update() throw  `high` `bug` `effort M`
- **Where:** apps/playground/src/components/cloud/ShareRoomModal.tsx:199-208, apps/playground/src/firebase/roomService.ts:198, :210-236, apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/RoomDto.ts:23
- **Problem:** `handleAddTeam` fabricates `user-${p.id}` uids and `…@team.local` emails, and `shareRoomWithTeam` writes members and pointers for accounts that cannot exist. Nobody gets access, yet the roster lists them as editors and `/user_rooms` fills with phantom uids. `color: team.color` and `photoURL: p.avatar` are often `undefined`, and RTDB `update()` throws on undefined values, so the whole share fails.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules:
    - `members/$m` `.validate` requires `root.child('usernames/'+newData.child('username').val()).val() === $memberUid`, which rejects phantom uids.
    - Teams:
      - Key: `$teamId.matches(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/)`.
      - Each `memberUids/$i` must be a room member in the same write: `newData.parent().parent().parent().parent().child('members/'+newData.val()).exists()`.
      - `color` is optional.
  - DTO: `toRoomMemberRecord(profile, role, extra?)` builds the member record and omits undefined fields. It has three callers: createRoom, shareRoomWithUser and shareRoomWithTeam/join.
  - Client → `fbsvc`/`roomsync`:
    - Resolve each person via `usernames/<normalizeUsername(p.username)>` → uid, then `public_profiles/<uid>`.
    - Skip people who don't resolve and report "N people are not on Jantt yet".
    - Never synthesize uids or emails.
- **Verify:**
  - `rules.test.ts`: denied when the owner writes `members/user-abc` with an unclaimed username, and for a team whose `memberUids` contains a non-member.
  - Manual: Add team with one Jantt user and one non-user → one member added, and a toast names the other.

#### [ ] RULES-01 · Link holders can read meta.secretKey and the member roster (room read-by-link is by design)  `medium` `rules-security` `effort L`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:31, :34, :45, :53, :57, :63, apps/playground/src/firebase/roomService.ts:59, :76, apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/RoomDto.ts:44
- **Problem:** `rooms/$roomId/.read: true` makes the entire room anonymously readable to anyone with the id: the plan, roster, presence and `meta/secretKey`. The nested `.read: true` rules are redundant because reads cascade. Read-by-link is the intended viewer model (ids are unguessable and `/rooms` is not listable). However, a room can never be members-only, the edit key leaks, and `isPublic` is dead code.
- **Fix:**
  - Decision: link-readable stays the default. Add `meta/visibility: 'link' | 'members'`; an absent value means `'link'`, so no migration is needed.
  - Rules:
    - `$roomId/.read: "data.child('meta/visibility').val() !== 'members' || (auth != null && auth.token.firebase.sign_in_provider === 'github.com' && data.child('members/'+auth.uid).exists())"`. It stays at `$roomId`, so whole-node `get`, `onValue` and transactions keep working (verifier note).
    - Delete every nested `.read`.
    - `meta/visibility` is owner-only, `.validate` `'link'|'members'`.
    - `meta/secretKey` gets `.validate: false`. Nothing new can be written, the owner can still delete it, and edit links are dropped (RULES-23).
  - DTO:
    - `RoomMetadata`: drop `isPublic` and `secretKey`; add `visibility?: RoomVisibility`.
  - Client → `fbsvc`:
    - `createRoom` stops generating `secretKey`.
    - The owner client deletes a legacy `meta/secretKey` when it opens the room.
    - Listeners handle cancel: after removal from a members-only room, `PERMISSION_DENIED` maps to a "This room is private" state.
  - Client → `roomsync`: Share popup toggle "Anyone with the link can view" / "Only invited people".
- **Verify:** `rules.test.ts`:
  - Allowed: anon `get(rooms/R)` with `link` visibility, and member get with `members`.
  - Denied: anon or non-member get with `members`; owner `set(meta/secretKey,'k')`; `set(meta/visibility,'public')`.

#### [ ] RULES-08 · Member records are unvalidated: a viewer can forge uid and trick the owner into deleting their own membership  `medium` `rules-security` `effort S`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:46, apps/playground/src/components/cloud/ShareRoomModal.tsx:90, :927, apps/playground/src/firebase/roomService.ts:290, :469-472
- **Problem:** Only `role` is constrained, so a self-joined viewer can store `{role:'viewer', uid:<ownerUid>}` under their own key. `ShareRoomModal` lists `Object.values(members)` and removes by `member.uid`. When the owner clicks Remove on the spammer, the owner's own membership is deleted instead. Autosave then aborts ("Permission denied"), the owner controls vanish and duplicate React keys corrupt the roster.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules, `members/$m` `.validate`:
    - On create, `hasChildren(['uid','username','role','joinedAt'])`.
    - `uid === $memberUid`.
    - `username` claimed by `$m`.
    - `displayName` ≤256; `photoURL` `https://` and ≤1024.
    - `role` per RULES-30.
    - `$other: false`.
  - Rules, self-writes: only join as viewer (RULES-26) or delete. Members cannot rewrite their own displayName or teamId (FBSVC-21).
  - Rules: `$roomId/.validate` forbids removing `members/<ownerUid>`.
  - DTO: `parseRoomMembers(raw)` returns `Record<uid, RoomMember>` with `uid` forced to the key and invalid entries dropped.
  - Client → `roomsync`:
    - Iterate `Object.entries`.
    - Use the key for remove, role change and the React key.
    - Never render Remove for `meta.ownerUid`.
- **Verify:**
  - `rules.test.ts`: denied for a viewer self-join with `uid: ownerUid`, a member rewriting their own `displayName`, and the owner removing `members/<ownerUid>`.
  - Static block: `parseRoomMembers({a:{uid:'b',…}}).a.uid === 'a'`.

#### [ ] RULES-09 · Any room owner can inject arbitrary pointers into any user's 'Shared with Me' list  `medium` `rules-security` `effort S`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:22-25, apps/playground/src/components/cloud/UserHubModal.tsx:274, :397-437, apps/playground/src/App.tsx:423
- **Problem:** Any room owner can write any body to `user_rooms/<anyUid>/shared/<theirRoom>`. There is no `.validate` and no membership check. Owners writing pointers is effectively the invite feature (verifier note); the defect is the unvalidated body. It allows spam with attacker-chosen title and owner name, multi-MB bodies re-downloaded by `listenToUserRooms`, and a body `roomId` that differs from the key, which opens and auto-joins a different room and makes Leave act on the wrong room.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules, `shared/$r`:
    - `.write` allows self (delete, or create together with one's own self-join) or the room owner.
    - `.validate`: role equals the newData root `rooms/$r/members/$uid/role` (only real members, in the same update), and role is `editor` or `viewer`.
    - Body is `{role, addedAt}` only (RULES-31), with `$other: false`.
  - Rules, `owned/$r`: `{role:'owner', addedAt}`, and `rooms/$r/meta/ownerUid === $uid`.
  - Client → `fbsvc` (`UserHubModal`) and `pgshell` (`App.tsx:423`): navigate by the snapshot key, never the body. Title and owner come from `rooms/$r/meta`.
- **Verify:** `rules.test.ts`:
  - Denied: the owner writes a pointer for a non-member uid; a pointer containing `title` or `roomId`.
  - Allowed: a pointer written in the same update as the member record.

#### [ ] RULES-10 · Presence is writable by any signed-in user in any room, with self-asserted fields and an isOwner badge  `medium` `rules-security` `effort S`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:56-60, apps/playground/src/components/layout/CloudBar.tsx:134, apps/playground/src/firebase/presenceService.ts:38-46, apps/playground/src/firebase/dtos/PresenceDto.ts:13
- **Problem:**
  - `presence/$uid` only checks `auth.uid === $uid`: there is no membership check and no `.validate`, and nonexistent rooms are accepted. Any GitHub user can inject fake collaborators into any room's avatar bar.
  - `isOwner` is never set by `trackRoomPresence` but is rendered by CloudBar, so only spoofers show "(Owner)".
  - Presence under an unused id creates `rooms/<id>`, which blocks that id's create clause and lets anyone claim its meta.
- **Fix:**
  - Rules: move presence to top-level `presence/$roomId/$uid/$connId`. Per-connection keys also fix multi-tab offline (ROOMSYNC-40, FBSVC-20).
    - `$roomId/.read`: signed-in GitHub member of `$roomId`.
    - `$roomId/.write`: owner delete only, used for room cleanup.
    - `$uid/.write`: `auth.uid === $uid && (!newData.exists() || root.child('rooms/'+$roomId+'/members/'+auth.uid).exists())`, plus owner delete when a member is removed.
    - Key: `$connId.matches(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$/)`.
    - `.validate`:
      - `hasChildren(['username','status','joinedAt'])`.
      - `username` claimed by `$uid`.
      - `status === 'online'`.
      - `joinedAt` and `lastSeen` are numbers `<= now`.
      - `displayName` ≤256; `photoURL` `https://` and ≤1024.
      - `$other: false`, which rejects `isOwner`.
  - Rules: delete `rooms/$roomId/presence`.
  - DTO:
    - `RoomPresence`: no `uid` (it is the key), no `isOwner`, ms timestamps.
    - `parsePresence(raw)` → `Array<RoomPresence & {uid}>`, deduplicated by uid.
    - Drop `presence` from `FullRoomPayload`.
  - Client → `fbsvc`: `presenceService` writes `presence/${roomId}/${uid}/${connId}` with `serverTimestamp()` and an `onDisconnect().remove()`.
  - Client → `roomsync`:
    - CloudBar derives "(Owner)" from `meta.ownerUid`.
    - Presence is its own subscription, separate from the room listener.
- **Verify:** `rules.test.ts`:
  - Denied: a non-member write; a member write containing `isOwner`; any read by anon.
  - A write in a nonexistent room is denied and `rooms/<id>` stays absent.
  - Allowed: a member read.

#### [ ] RULES-13 · Consolidated room-rules redesign (overlaps #0, #2, #7, #14, #16)  `medium` `architecture` `effort L`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:29-66 (notably :31, :32, :37, :40, :48)
- **Problem:** One compound room-level `.write` cascades over every child, the room root has a public `.read`, and only three `.validate` nodes exist. There is no visibility concept, no `$other` guard and no size cap; presence lives inside the room node, and the secret shares the readable meta. Patching clauses one at a time keeps reintroducing escalations, as 52ec345 did.
- **Fix:** Rewrite the `rooms` subtree in one pass, exactly as in the Notes contract table. This task is the umbrella for RULES-01/03/08/10/15/16/17/20/26/30.
  - `$roomId`:
    - `.read` per RULES-01, kept at this level (whole-node reads and transactions need it).
    - `.write` allows create-by-owner or owner only.
    - `.validate`: `meta` present and the owner member record preserved.
    - `$other: false`.
  - `meta`:
    - Owner writes it.
    - Editors may write only `revision`, `contentHash`, `updatedAt`, `taskCount`, `noteCount`.
    - `roomId === $roomId`; `ownerUid` immutable; `ownerUsername` claimed by ownerUid; `visibility`; `theme` ≤64.
    - `$other: false`.
  - `members/$m`, `teams/$t`, `banned/$u`: owner writes them; self may join as viewer or leave.
  - `data`: owner or editor, no editor delete, structural caps (RULES-17).
  - RTDB has no macros. Repeat the same predicate strings verbatim (owner, member, editor, GitHub provider), so reviewers can diff them by eye. The static test fails on any fixed-shape node without `$other: false`.
- **Verify:** every room row of `database.rules.test.md` is green in the emulator.

#### [ ] RULES-14 · Consolidated identity-path redesign (overlaps #1, #5, #6, #8, #17, #18)  `medium` `architecture` `effort M`
- **Where:** database.rules.json:3-28 (notably :3, :10, :16)
- **Problem:** `/users` and `/usernames` are world-readable with no `.validate`, and `/usernames` has no format or one-per-uid limit. `user_rooms/owned` accepts any body, and shared pointers are writable by any room owner for any uid. Only `auth != null` is ever checked, never the sign-in provider.
